ten.games_per_set_distribution.label: Games-per-set distribution from the pair's hold rates
ten.games_per_set_distribution.mechanism: The mass over {6,7,8,9,10,12,13} games for a set is a function of the two hold probabilities.
ten.games_per_set_distribution.rationale: Totals are most sensitive to the discrete masses at 12 and 13 games, which a continuous model misses and which depend on the hold levels in a nonlinear way.
ten.games_per_set_distribution.measurement: For hold probabilities h_A and h_B from adjusted serve/return (A and B alternating serve, first server randomised), compute by dynamic programming the set-score PMF over 6-0 .. 7-6; calibrate to the empirical frequency of set scores from Sackmann by bins of (h_A+h_B)/2 and |h_A-h_B| with kernel smoothing and shrinkage n/(n+60) to the model PMF. Output the PMF of games per set and P(tiebreak). As-of: serve statistics before the match.
free_sources: Sackmann score strings and serve counts

ten.retirement_games_completed_profile.label: Completed games at retirement
ten.retirement_games_completed_profile.mechanism: The count of games completed when a retirement ends the match.
ten.retirement_games_completed_profile.rationale: Totals markets settle on completed games, so an interrupted match gives a truncated count; the over side can be settled if the count already exceeds the strike.
ten.retirement_games_completed_profile.measurement: From Sackmann score strings with RET compute games completed by tour and best_of; fit a distribution with covariates (age, round, heat flag) and shrink with n/(n+30); output P(count>k | retirement) for each strike k.
free_sources: Sackmann score strings with RET

ten.player_games_residual.label: Player persistent games-per-match residual
ten.player_games_residual.mechanism: A player's matches end up longer or shorter than a rating-based model predicts, persistently across opponents.
ten.player_games_residual.rationale: Style traits (patient baseline play vs aggressive first-strike tennis) show up as residual match length beyond hold and rating; the existing return-style input is a descriptive profile, not a measured residual.
ten.player_games_residual.measurement: Compute residual_i = games in match minus model expectation (from adjusted hold rates), averaged over the last 40 matches with half-life 9 months, shrunk with n/(n+20) toward 0; test persistence by split-sample correlation before use. As-of date: day before match.
free_sources: Sackmann scores and serve counts

ten.decider_format_tail.label: Deciding-set format and tail probability
ten.decider_format_tail.mechanism: The deciding set can end at 6-6 with a 7-point tiebreak, at 6-6 with a 10-point tiebreak, at 12-12, or only by a two-game margin.
ten.decider_format_tail.rationale: The right tail of totals depends on the final-set rule by event and year; Davis Cup and some tour events differ from the majors.
ten.decider_format_tail.measurement: Event-year lookup of deciding rule; probability of a deciding set exceeding 13 games from the DP model under that rule (0 for tiebreak at 6-6, geometric for advantage sets). Include the format effective date. As-of: official rulebook for the event year.

ten.round_robin_group_structure.label: Round-robin group structure and tie-break rules
ten.round_robin_group_structure.mechanism: In round-robin finals, advancement depends on group composition, results and tie-break rules, not on a knockout path.
ten.round_robin_group_structure.rationale: ATP Finals, WTA Finals and Next Gen Finals use groups; the probability of advancing is a function of the three-match group and tie-break rules (wins, head-to-head, set ratio, game ratio), and alternates replace withdrawals.
ten.round_robin_group_structure.measurement: Simulate the group of four: 6 matches each with win probabilities from surface ratings at the event (indoor hard), record wins, sets and games; apply the official tie-break order; probability of advancing and of winning the event = P(advance) * product of semifinal and final probabilities; handle alternates as additional entrants with replacement probabilities. Rules from the event rulebook for the year; as-of group draw.

ten.withdrawal_cascade_effect.label: Withdrawal cascade through the bracket
ten.withdrawal_cascade_effect.mechanism: A withdrawal changes the bracket: the opponent gets a walkover (rest), a lucky loser enters, and the path of other players shifts.
ten.withdrawal_cascade_effect.rationale: The stage rule says a player who qualifies for the final but does not play still pays, so withdrawals at different points settle differently, and a withdrawal reshuffles the title probabilities of everyone else.
ten.withdrawal_cascade_effect.measurement: For each possible withdrawal, recompute title and stage probabilities with the replacement rules (lucky loser from qualifying draw with ratings, opponent's walkover with rest credit); weight by an empirical day-level withdrawal rate by round taken from W/O score rows (no timestamp; see tw_withdrawal_vintage and tw_sackmann_access), and treat any horizon-specific weighting as available only from forward own-capture; output the sensitivity of each player's title probability to the top-8 players' withdrawals.

ten.round_upset_calibration.label: Round-by-round upset calibration by seed band
ten.round_upset_calibration.mechanism: Empirical upset frequency by round, seed band and surface to calibrate the path simulation.
ten.round_upset_calibration.rationale: A model that multiplies match probabilities can be miscalibrated for early-round upsets and late-round parity; the calibration table is a data-driven check.
ten.round_upset_calibration.measurement: From Sackmann results compute by round and seed-difference bin the favourite's win frequency relative to the Elo-implied probability; fit a logistic correction with round dummies; shrink to 0 with n/(n+100); apply to the simulation. As-of: before event.

ten.in_event_rating_update.label: In-event rating and form updating
ten.in_event_rating_update.mechanism: As a tournament proceeds, each round's performance (serve and return numbers, not just win/loss) updates a player's strength estimate.
ten.in_event_rating_update.rationale: The title probability before round four should use information from rounds one to three; a dominant straight-set run is evidence about current form and health that pre-event ratings do not have.
ten.in_event_rating_update.measurement: After each match compute performance residual = (observed dominance ratio minus expected from ratings), shrink with a weight k=0.15 per match for the next-round estimate; clip at +/- 40 Elo; apply decay to zero over 10 days. As-of: after each completed match. The constants k=0.15, the +/-40 Elo clip and the 10-day decay are initial placeholders, to be fitted on past events by out-of-sample log loss of next-round match predictions, not validated values; the sign of the fatigue interaction is a hypothesis (a long match can signal both load and form).
free_sources: Sackmann CSV (serve stats by match, when available)

ten.short_format_rules.label: Next Gen Finals short-format scoring rules
ten.short_format_rules.mechanism: Short sets (first to four games, tiebreak at 3-3), no-ad scoring and a best-of-five sets match change the point-to-match map, so favourite probabilities and round-robin set/game ratios differ from standard best-of-three tour matches.
ten.short_format_rules.rationale: KXATPNEXTGEN is a live series and the Next Gen Finals use a shortened format; applying standard-set hold-to-match conversion misstates match win probability and the set/game-ratio tiebreaks that decide round-robin advancement.
ten.short_format_rules.measurement: Code the event format from the current-year rulebook (sets to win, games per set, tiebreak score, ad or no-ad, let rule). Convert spw to the game hold probability with the no-ad formula (the receiver wins the single deciding point at 3-3, so hold = sum over scores of the point-win probabilities with one deciding point), then to a first-to-four set with a tiebreak at 3-3 by a DP over game scores, then to best-of-five sets. Use per-player spw/rpw with a short-format variance inflation estimated from past Next Gen Finals sets (pooled shrinkage n/(n+40) toward the standard-format model). As-of: rulebook publication before the event; rules change between years so the year is part of the key.

ten.unretirement_reentry_status.label: Re-entry status of a retired player (testing-pool notice and entry route)
ten.unretirement_reentry_status.mechanism: A player who has retired can only compete again after re-registering for anti-doping testing with advance notice and obtaining a main-draw place by wildcard or special/protected ranking.
ten.unretirement_reentry_status.rationale: For a comeback-from-retirement contract the binding constraint is administrative and personal, not physical recovery: the WADA Code return-from-retirement rule requires written notice to the anti-doping authority months before competing, and with no ranking the player needs wildcards; a public notice is a near-necessary leading indicator that sharply separates a near-zero probability from a material one. Subtle: notice lists may not be public, and doubles or exhibition play can precede singles.
ten.unretirement_reentry_status.measurement: State variable as of the market timestamp with values {no public re-entry step, testing-pool re-registration reported (date), wildcard or protected-ranking entry announced (event, date), entered in an acceptance list}; earliest eligible competition date = notice date + required notice period (six months under the WADA Code rule, to be checked against the current ITIA Tennis Anti-Doping Programme); P(compete by window end) = 0 before the earliest eligible date, otherwise a hazard estimated from historical un-retirements (e.g. Clijsters, Hingis, Wozniacki) with n<20 so shrink heavily toward a judgemental prior.

Reputable news reports

game_side.mechanism: Tennis side markets (match winner, set/game spread, exact set score, in-play game winner) are determined by a hierarchical point process: serve and return point-win probabilities by surface give hold/break probabilities, which give game, set and match outcomes. The skill gap enters through opponent-adjusted serve/return ratings; format (best-of-3 vs 5) amplifies the favourite; fitness, fatigue and conditions modify point probabilities; and retirement/walkover rules decide what happens when the match does not finish. Sharp closing odds already encode most public information, so incremental value is in late fitness news, retirement-aware settlement and cross-market consistency.
game_side.target: Winner or score outcome of a tennis match (or set/game) as settled by the contract wording, including retirement handling.

The model is a joint simulation with a shared player state and the draws of each event.

game_total.mechanism: Total games and total sets markets follow from the distribution of the match: closeness (rating gap), hold probabilities (tiebreak frequency), format (bo3/bo5, final-set rule) and match-form dependence. Longer matches occur when players are evenly matched and when both hold serve well (tiebreaks), shorter when one dominates. The distribution is lumpy (discrete game counts, tiebreak jump to 13 games) so rungs have structure that must be priced as a ladder.

Before the draw, probabilities average over draw randomness; after, path difficulty dominates. match_winner.label: Match winner
match_winner.target: Winner of the match, with retirement/walkover per contract wording.
match_winner.mechanism: Match-win probability is a function of the serve/return point-win edge on the actual surface, amplified by the number of sets, adjusted for fitness, fatigue and conditions, and tied to settlement rules for retirements. Elo by surface gives a robust base; opponent-adjusted serve/return gives pair-specific hold/break; the market's sharp close is the benchmark.

inputs.why: Sets the base probability: a surface-blended Elo gap converts to a win probability, and the surface weighting is what separates a clay specialist from a hard-court player with the same overall rating.

Match odds are really the pair's point-win rates on serve and return; adjusting each player's raw rates for the quality of opponents faced shows how this specific pairing plays, which a single rating hides.
Converts point-level serve/return strength into game, set and match probability through the hold/break chain, so a small per-point edge is amplified in a best-of-five and diluted in a best-of-three.

Best-of-five gives the stronger player more sets to express a per-point edge, so the same rating gap implies a more lopsided winner price than in best-of-three; the contract's format must be known before pricing.
An injured or ill player wins less and may retire; the price moves only when the status is public, so the timestamp of the report matters more than the report itself.
Long previous matches, a short turnaround and late-night finishes lower serve speed and movement; the effect is largest in later rounds and best-of-five events.
Fast courts, altitude and indoor air raise hold rates and favour big servers, while slow clay favours returners and rallying; the effect scales with how different the two players' styles are.

Head-to-head only adds information once serve/return rates and handedness are controlled; a lopsided history with a small sample is mostly noise, but a stylistic mismatch (big server vs elite returner) persists.
Returning, young and low-sample players have wide rating error; the winner price should be shrunk toward 50% less aggressively for them, and the market often over-trusts a single recent result.
Whether a retirement or walkover settles the winner contract as a win, void or loss changes which side is worth buying when one player is hurt; the exact contract wording decides the payoff.
The sportsbook closing line is the efficient-market benchmark; any model must beat it, not just predict outcomes, and its timestamp vs the Kalshi quote determines whether the comparison is fair.

Choosing how to remove the book's margin (proportional, power, Shin) changes the implied probability of longshots by a few points; favourite-longshot bias in tennis lines is exactly where a mispricing study would look.
Raw serve-point and return-point win rates by surface are the building blocks of the pair model; their sample size per surface (few grass matches) limits how far they can be trusted.
Recent results relative to rating expectation capture slumps and hot streaks only if they exceed what rating updates already absorb; most apparent form is regression to the rating.
Break chances come mostly from second-serve points; a player with a weak second serve against a strong returner loses more games than their first-serve numbers imply.
Lets a player's thin clay or grass record borrow information from similar surfaces, which matters most early in the season and for players switching surface.
A left-hander's serve patterns and ad-court slice are unusual to face, and the opponent's lack of practice against them shows in break rates, but the edge is small and shrinks with sample size.
Long-haul travel and time shifts affect the first days of an event; it matters for early rounds after intercontinental swings and is largely gone by the quarterfinals.
Rain delays and overnight suspensions change momentum, order of play and rest, and can leave a match unfinished past the contract's settlement window.
Swaps a three-way categorical surface label for a continuous pace response so the winner price separates specialists at fast vs slow hard courts.
Corrects a systematic scale mismatch that only affects Challenger/lower-tier winner contracts, where Kalshi lists many matches.
Winner contracts on doubles pairs cannot be priced from singles ratings; the dedicated series are listed and their pairs change week to week.
Prevents applying tour-match calibration to exhibitions where effort and format differ from tour rules.
Gives the probability the contract voids to fair price rather than resolving, and flags when a price move reflects a withdrawal.

mechanism_review.summary: A tennis match winner is the end of a nested counting process. Each service point is won by the server with probability that depends on that specific server-returner pair on that court: the server's serve quality, the returner's return quality, the court speed and ball, and the player's physical state on the day. Points aggregate into games through a deuce-amplifying hold function, games into sets through six-all tiebreak rules, and sets into the match through the best-of-three or best-of-five target, so a small point-level edge becomes a large winner edge. Day-level form shocks shared across points create overdispersion that lowers the favourite's edge relative to an i.i.d. chain. Before any of that happens a participation gate decides whether the contract has a match at all, and after play starts a retirement hazard can truncate the match before the count completes. The winner market is also the most liquid one, which makes it the anchor the other tennis archetypes are priced against.

stages.name: Participation and start gate
stages.description: Before the point model matters, a match must be played. Withdrawals after the draw, walkovers, late lucky-loser swaps and rain postponements decide whether the contract resolves at a fair price or runs to a result. The gate is almost entirely a function of news timing, order-of-play publication and entry-list status, and it is correlated with the injury state that also lowers a player's point-win rate if he does start.
stages.distribution: Bernoulli per player with a hazard that spikes in the 24 hours before order of play; strongly clustered by player-injury state and tournament round.

stages.name: Latent strength on this specific court
stages.description: Each player has a latent ability on the match's court that is neither overall Elo nor raw surface Elo: it is a continuous function of court speed and ball behaviour. A big server's latent strength rises with court speed while a counter-puncher's falls, so two players with equal clay Elo are not equal at a fast indoor hard event. The estimate must also carry honest uncertainty for returners, juniors and players who recently moved between Challenger and tour level. For the three doubles series (KXATPDOUBLES, KXWTADOUBLES, KXATPCHALLENGERDOUBLES) the unit of strength is the pair, not either player: ten.doubles_pair_strength (doubles ratings, partnership continuity) replaces the singles rating, and for KXTENNISEXHIBITION the rating gap is shrunk for format and effort (ten.exhibition_format_effort) because exhibition results carry little competitive signal.
stages.distribution: Gaussian-like latent ability with heteroscedastic uncertainty; uncertainty is heavy-tailed for players with fewer than about 30 recent tour matches or after a layoff.

stages.name: Pair-specific serve and return point model
stages.description: Match probability is generated by two numbers: A's probability of winning a point on his serve against B's return and B's on his serve against A's return. They come from each player's serve quality and return quality relative to the tour average on this surface, plus pair interactions such as a big lefty slice serve into a weak ad-court backhand return. The pair of serve-point probabilities, not the gap in overall rating, drives games, sets and the match.
stages.distribution: Two correlated binomial rates; the two spw values are individually well estimated (0.60-0.70 on tour) but their difference is small, so estimation error of 1-2 points of spw already swings match probability by several percent.

stages.name: Day-of physical and scheduling modifiers
stages.description: Fatigue from the previous rounds, short turnaround, time-zone shift and in-tournament medical history move the two point-win probabilities down by small amounts on the day. These are modifiers to the s3 rates, not additional strength measures, and most of them are only observable as match minutes, rest days and public injury reports.
stages.distribution: Small mean shifts (about 0.5-2 points of spw) with a fat left tail for visibly injured players; correlated across rounds within a tournament.

stages.name: Points to games to sets to match with shared day shocks
stages.description: The two spw values are pushed through the game-hold function, set tiebreak rules and the sets-to-win target. A latent match-level form shock shared across points makes set outcomes positively correlated, which flattens the favourite's edge versus an i.i.d. chain, while best-of-five gives the stronger player more points to express the edge and doubles formats with match tiebreaks do the opposite.
stages.distribution: Discrete nested counts: games are geometric-like around deuce, sets are bounded random walks, match is a first-to-n race; overdispersion from the shared shock raises 2-1 and 3-2 frequency.

stages.name: Mid-match termination and settlement
stages.description: Retirements truncate the count: the player who is injured or physically spent stops, and the tour record gives the match to his opponent. This converts a stage-5 loss into a settled loss or an ambiguous outcome depending on wording. The hazard is higher in best-of-five, in heat, and for players who began the match visibly impaired, and it is the only stage where the winning side is chosen by an event unrelated to point-win rate.
stages.distribution: Rare absorbing event (roughly 1-3% of tour matches) concentrated in the trailing, injured player; tail risk is far larger for a favourite carrying a known injury.

stages.name: Named-round winner: reaching the round and winning it
stages.description: The eight tournament-named series (ATP Acapulco, Monte Carlo, Miami, Madrid; WTA Indian Wells, Miami, Madrid, Dubai) settle on the named player being 'a winner of the semifinal/final'. Once the pairing is fixed this is the s3-s6 match model for that round. If the market is listed earlier, the probability is P(reach the named round) times P(win it | opponent distribution), computed by draw simulation over the remaining bracket with seed-dependent opponents, accumulated fatigue and per-round walkover hazard, so the named player's draw quarter matters as much as their rating.
stages.distribution: Product of per-round Bernoulli survivals along a draw path, mixed over the opponent distribution in each round; strongly right-skewed across players (most mass on top seeds) with negative dependence between players in the same section.

coaching_scheme.note: Tennis has no in-match substitution, rotation or play-calling decision that a pre-match variable can observe; coaching-staff changes act slowly through the rating and are indistinguishable from form at the single-match horizon.

pace_volume.note: A winner market is not a count: serve-point volume enters only through the best-of-three/five and match-tiebreak format, which is already carried by ten.format and the points-to-match transformation in ten.hold_break (a model component, not an extra measurable). No separate pace or volume input would change P(win).

officiating_rules.note: The official only affects the winner through line-call overrules and code violations, whose effect on a single match winner is below estimation noise; rules differences (final-set format, no-ad) are carried by ten.format instead.

contract_review.settlement_definition: Two contract objects share this archetype. (1) Single-match winner (KXATPMATCH, KXWTAMATCH, KXATPCHALLENGERMATCH, KXWTACHALLENGERMATCH, KXATPDOUBLES, KXWTADOUBLES, KXATPCHALLENGERDOUBLES, KXTENNISEXHIBITION with rules; KXATPGAME, KXWTAGAME title only): 'If Casper Ruud wins the Casper Ruud vs Carlos Alcaraz professional tennis match ... after a ball has been played, then the market resolves to Yes'. A match that never starts resolves to a fair price and a postponed match stays open up to two weeks; the sampled text has no retirement sentence before the disclaimer, so the opponent of a retiring player winning is tour convention, not text. (2) Named-round winner (KXATPAMT, KXATPMC, KXATPMIA, KXATPMAD, KXWTAIWO, KXWTAMIA, KXWTAMAD, KXWTADDF, all recovered from archived 2025 markets): 'If Jack Draper is a 2025 winner of the final of ATP Madrid, then the market resolves to Yes', with semifinal variants. These carry no secondary text, so walkover, retirement and non-occurrence treatment is unstated, and if listed before the pairing is set the event includes reaching the round. No overtime concept exists; source of truth is not named.
contract_review.settlement_data_source: Governing-league match result (ATP/WTA/ITF official score and draw); the exact named source is not stated in the sampled rules text.
variants_and_edge_cases: Retirement after the first ball: the sampled winner rules say nothing about it (the retirement sentence appears only in the set/game/totals variants and is cut off in the sample), so the settlement of a retiring-favourite match is CONTRACT_AMBIGUOUS.

Doubles series (KXWTADOUBLES, KXATPDOUBLES, KXATPCHALLENGERDOUBLES) settle a pair; doubles use no-ad scoring and a 10-point match tiebreak in place of a third set, which compresses the match and raises the variance of the winner outcome per point of edge.
Lower-level matches (Challenger) have thinner data, sometimes no live scoring feed, so the 'after a ball has been played' trigger and the settlement source can lag the real result.

Scope: these inputs are pre-match only. KXATPMATCH/KXATPCHALLENGERMATCH trade during play (sampled markets show both active and finalized status), but in-match state (score, server, medical timeout, live retirement hazard) is not an input here; it belongs to game_winner_inplay-type state inputs and no live-state input list exists for match-winner markets.

Series set after the reconciliation: eighteen series. Ten single-match series (eight with rules: KXATPMATCH, KXWTAMATCH, KXATPCHALLENGERMATCH, KXWTACHALLENGERMATCH, KXATPDOUBLES, KXWTADOUBLES, KXATPCHALLENGERDOUBLES, KXTENNISEXHIBITION; KXATPGAME/KXWTAGAME title only) and eight tournament-named round-winner series with rules (KXATPAMT, KXATPMC, KXATPMIA, KXATPMAD, KXWTAIWO, KXWTAMIA, KXWTAMAD, KXWTADDF).

Named-round winner series ('a 2025 winner of the final/semifinal of X'): mechanically identical to the KXATPIWO/KXATPIT/KXATPMCO round-winner series filed under tournament_winner_futures; if listed before the round's pairing is known, Yes needs reaching and winning the round, and a walkover win in the named round or a withdrawal before it is unaddressed by any text.

set_and_game_spreads.label: Set and game spreads
set_and_game_spreads.target: Game or set differential of a player relative to a handicap line.
set_and_game_spreads.mechanism: Spreads depend on the distribution of the game (or set) differential, not just the win probability: it needs the hold/break probabilities of both players, the match format and the lopsidedness distribution. Push rules and half-point lines matter. Ladders of spread lines must be consistent with the match-winner market and with each other.

inputs.why: The game margin is the sum of break differentials over sets; a player who breaks more and holds more wins by larger margins, and the hold/break chain converts that into a spread distribution.
Spread cover depends on the specific pair's break rates, so opponent-adjusted components replace each player's raw averages.
The rating gap sets the expected margin; the mapping from Elo gap to expected game margin is roughly linear in the middle and flattens at the extremes.
Fat tails in the margin come from 6-0 and 6-1 sets; players with high lopsided-set rates cover large handicaps more often than a normal approximation says.
Sets are not independent: a player who wins the first set tends to win the second, so margins have a heavier spread than independent-set models give.
A handicap of -4.5 games means very different things in best-of-three and best-of-five; the set count and final-set rule set how large margins can get.
WTA matches have more breaks and smaller expected margins than ATP for the same rating gap, so ATP-calibrated models mis-size women's spreads.
A mid-match retirement leaves a partial margin that usually settles the favourite's cover as lost or void.
Whether a retired match settles the spread on games played, as a win for the other player, or as void changes the value of the cover side.
Spread rungs must be monotone and consistent with the winner price; violations indicate stale quotes rather than mispricing.
Game margins widen against a player with a weak second serve because they lose a higher share of their service games.
Pooling across surfaces stabilises margin estimates for players with few matches on the current surface.
Tired players lose more games late in matches, so fatigue widens margins in the final set more than it changes the winner.
Connects the hold model directly to the spread strike so mean and strike can be compared with the right variance.
Gives the exact discrete tail probabilities that a Gaussian approximation mis-sizes at half-point strikes.
Prevents treating the games spread as a shifted winner probability when a sizeable share of wins are close.
Provides the explicit within-set clustering that underlies heavy margin tails.
Quantifies the retirement tail for a spread contract whose retirement clause is cut off in the sample.

Shared definition with set_winner_and_any_set (single definition of the set-count and straight-set mass); supplies the set-differential rungs of KXATPSSPREAD (3-0/3-1 in best-of-five, 2-0 in best-of-three) that this archetype owns by target.

interactions.hypothesis: Game-differential tails come from lopsided sets, whose frequency exceeds iid predictions.
A retiring favourite leads in games but loses the match; settlement rules determine whether the spread counts.
Higher WTA break rates make spreads less sensitive to hold probability and more to return.

The expected margin scales with the number of games played, so the same hold gap produces a mean margin about 1.6 times larger in best-of-five than in best-of-three, but the straight-set stopping rule limits the increase.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare the realised mean D per hold gap bin for bo3 and bo5 and test the ratio against the expected 5/3 games ratio adjusted for set counts.

interactions.hypothesis: Bagels and breadsticks concentrate in matches with a large rating gap, so the tail of margin grows faster than the mean as the gap increases; a player-level lopsided rate adds to this for the favourite.
interactions.how_to_test: Plot P(D>=8) against rating gap bins split by the favourite's lopsided-set rate.

interactions.hypothesis: With low hold levels (WTA) both players break often, so the margin variance is high but its mean depends on return strength more than on serve; with high holds (ATP) tiebreaks cap the margin.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate separate margin-vs-hold-gap slopes for ATP and WTA and test equality.

interactions.hypothesis: In retirement matches the margin is truncated: either the contract settles on games played (favouring the leader's cover) or leaves the market for the unconditional clause, flipping which side of the strike a late-leading favourite lands on.
interactions.how_to_test: For historical retirements, compute D at stoppage and compare cover outcomes under both settlement rules.

nonlinearities.why: The mean margin is linear in the hold gap but the variance falls as hold levels increase because tiebreak sets cap the margin at 1; the strike probability is therefore not linear in the gap.
A small increase in a player's bagel rate increases P(D>=8) disproportionately because margins of 6 and 5 in one set stack with another lopsided set.

nonlinearities.shape: saturating mapping from rating gap to expected margin
nonlinearities.why: Rating gap converts to games margin roughly linearly in the middle but flattens for very large gaps because the loser still wins about two games per set.

mechanism_review.summary: The games spread is the signed sum of per-set game margins, so it is a continuous-looking but discrete quantity driven by who holds and who breaks. Per game played the expected margin equals the hold-rate gap, so over the roughly ten games of a tour set it is about ten times the gap (twelve times only over a fixed 12-game window, which overstates the set margin), which means the mean margin depends on the difference of two hold probabilities, while the variance depends on their level and on how often tiebreaks and bagels occur. The winner market is only a coarse projection of this: a match can be won by a player whose games differential is negative (a 7-6 0-6 7-6 pattern) and a favourite who retires still carries the margin accumulated so far. Sets are linked by a latent day-level shock, so margins are heavier-tailed than independent-set models imply, and the match's length is endogenous (a straight-set win stops play early and removes games that would have added margin to either side). The settlement layer adds a mismatch: the contract refers to the full match, while a retirement may truncate the count at the moment the leader or the trailer stops.

stages.name: Hold-rate gap per player
stages.description: The expected games margin per set is proportional to the gap between the two hold probabilities, since each player's wins come from their own service games and from the other player's lost service games. Opponent-adjusted serve and return components give the hold rates for this pair on this court, and the same two numbers also govern the variance of the margin.
stages.distribution: Continuous rates near 0.6-0.9 for tour holds; the margin mean is a linear function of the hold gap (E[games in set] times the gap, about 10 rather than 12 per tour set, see ten.hold_gap_expected_margin) and noise shrinks only slowly with sample size.

stages.name: Per-set margin distribution with tiebreak discreteness
stages.description: Each set ends at 6-0 to 6-4 (margins 6 to 2), 7-5 (2), or 7-6 (1). A tiebreak caps the margin at one game regardless of how dominant the winner was in the tiebreak itself. This creates a probability mass at margin 1 for sets between holders, a mass at 2 for sets with one break, and a thin tail at 5-6 for bagels and breadsticks.
stages.distribution: Discrete support {6,5,4,3,2,1} with heavy mass at 2 and 1 for evenly matched servers; lopsided sets form a separate tail component.

stages.name: Serial dependence between games and sets
stages.description: Games are not independent: a player who has just been broken holds less often and sometimes breaks back; the favourite serving to stay in a set is under different pressure than a game at 2-2. At the set level the day-level form shock links sets. Together they thicken the tails of the margin relative to an independent model.
stages.distribution: Positive serial correlation in game results within a set (small, around 0.05-0.1) and between sets (larger); heavier tails than a sum of independent binomials.

stages.name: Endogenous match length and format
stages.description: The number of sets played depends on the outcomes: a 6-3 6-2 win ends play at two sets, whereas a 6-3 3-6 6-2 win accumulates a third set whose margin may be positive or negative. Best-of-five gives more sets for margin to compound. Because games are only counted while play continues, margin variance and mean are functions of match length that is itself chosen by the outcomes. The set spread KXATPSSPREAD ('wins by over 1.5 sets') is read directly off this stage: it is the named player's straight-set or one-set-dropped win in best-of-five (3-0, 3-1), i.e. P(win) times P(at most one set lost | win) from ten.set_count_distribution_by_edge, which is why the set-count input sits here.
stages.distribution: Mixture over set counts; the straight-set branch has margin concentrated near +5 to +8 for the winner, the decider branch has margin near 0 to +3.

stages.name: Tour, gender and level differences
stages.description: WTA matches have more breaks, so the same rating gap converts into a smaller expected games margin and a different distribution of 3-set outcomes; Challenger and ITF levels have a larger spread of player quality and more dispersion in margin. A model fit on ATP tour data will mis-size women's or lower-level spreads.
stages.distribution: Tour-level shifts in the average hold probability (for example about 0.80 for ATP vs 0.65 for WTA) and in the dispersion of margin.

stages.name: Retirement truncation of the margin
stages.description: If a player retires, the games differential stops accumulating at the moment of retirement. The retiring player is usually trailing, so the truncated margin is typically positive for the opponent and often well below a full-match margin; the rung that settles depends on the truncated clause.
stages.distribution: Rare truncation event, concentrated in the trailing player; the margin at retirement is usually 2-6 games in the opponent's favour.

role_personnel.note: A singles game spread involves two fixed players and no lineup or role; participation changes void to a fair price before play and are not a role variable.

coaching_scheme.note: Tactical and coaching adjustments have no pre-match observable at the margin level; their effect appears indirectly in serial dependence between sets.

environment.note: Court speed, altitude, indoor state and ball condition shift the hold level, hence tiebreak mass and margin variance; ten.venue_speed_history (event hold and ace history from match data) is the available proxy and ten.court_cond the condition flags, both shared with the totals and set records. A verified public per-event pace index is still missing (sp_court_pace).

situational_schedule_motivation.note: Recent minutes, sets and five-set exposure (ten.workload_minutes) define fatigue concretely; ten.fatigue is WEAK for the margin on its own so the defined load quantity is attached.

contract_review.settlement_definition: KXATPGSPREAD is a binary on the games differential across the whole match: 'If the game differential in favor of Luca Van Assche across the full match is above 1.5 games', then Yes (strike_type greater, floor_strike 1.5; the title words it as 'win at least 1.5 more games'). The differential is player A's total games minus player B's total games summed over every set including tiebreak sets (the sampled text does not say how a 7-6 tiebreak set or a 10-point match tiebreak/super-tiebreak enters the differential; counting 7-6 as one game for the winner is an assumption); the half-point strike means there is no push. A match that never starts resolves to a fair price; postponed matches stay open for up to two weeks; the retirement clause says that markets that can be unconditionally settled from play already completed settle on it, but the sampled sentence is cut off. The set spread KXATPSSPREAD ('wins by over 1.5 sets', strike_type greater, floor 1.5) is now filed here: Yes only for a 3-0 or 3-1 win in best-of-five (2-0 in best-of-three), driven by ten.set_count_distribution_by_edge; its retirement clause is cut off in the same way.
contract_review.settlement_data_source: Governing-league recorded set scores summed to games per player; the sampled rules text does not name a vendor.
variants_and_edge_cases: Title and rule wording differ: the title says 'win at least 1.5 more games' while the rule says 'above 1.5 games'; with a half-point strike they are equivalent, but a whole-number strike (if listed) would need a push rule that is not visible.

Retirement mid-match: the differential at the moment of stopping can be positive for the player who is about to be recorded the loser, so a retiring player who led on games can still be the one whose games differential is above the strike; the sampled clause does not say whether the incomplete match is settled on games played.

Best-of-three versus best-of-five and tiebreak or advantage deciding sets change the number of sets and games over which margin accumulates. An advantage final set (abolished at the majors since 2022, but the format must be checked per event) lengthens the set without widening its margin: once past 6-4 it can only end at a two-game margin (8-6, 12-10), so it adds games, not margin tail; a single set's margin is never above 6.

Two live series with rules sit here (KXATPGSPREAD game differential, KXATPSSPREAD set differential, both ATP men's); no WTA spread series was found, so the WTA treatment (more breaks, smaller margins) is unobserved. A retirement in a set-spread match leaves a 1-0 or 2-0 set lead short of a completed 'win by over 1.5 sets', and the cut-off clause does not say how it settles.

nonlinearities.shape: S-shaped in edge for straight sets
nonlinearities.why: P(straight-sets win) rises slowly for even matches, steeply for moderate favourites, then saturates near the favourite's match win probability.

mechanism_review.summary: A set is a race to six games with a two-game margin and a tiebreak at six-all, so a set-level win probability is generated by the two hold probabilities and by the first server. Set markets differ from match markets because a set has fewer points and a larger share of noise: the first-set win probability of a 75% match favourite is much closer to 50%. The set-winner and any-set contracts are transforms of the same sequence of set outcomes: a named set is a marginal over the other sets and 'any set' is one minus the opponent's straight-sets probability (total sets and set spread, now in sibling archetypes, are further transforms of the same sequence). Both depend on how the outcome of one set shifts the next, which is where momentum, a day-level form shock, fatigue and tactical adjustment sit, and where the conditional probability that a set exists (a third set only if 1-1) becomes part of the price. Two further layers sit outside the point model: the possibility that a set is interrupted by a retirement, and the ambiguity about an unplayed set.

stages.name: Set existence and format
stages.description: The first question is whether the named set will be played at all. A third set in best-of-three exists only after 1-1; a fifth set in best-of-five only after 2-2; the existence indicator is exactly what the set-count distribution supplies. Format therefore turns a named later-set winner into a conditional contract, and KXATPANYSET into one minus the opponent's straight-sets mass.
stages.distribution: Bernoulli existence indicators with a cascade structure; the probability of reaching set 5 is a product of three set outcomes.

stages.name: Set-one probability with first-server adjustment
stages.description: Set 1 is the baseline: the pair's hold and break rates give P(A wins set 1), shaded by who serves first and by the chance of a tiebreak. First-set probabilities are noisier than match probabilities, so favourites are shaded toward 0.5 and the shading is larger on fast courts and for big servers.
stages.distribution: Binomial-like around 0.45-0.70; the tiebreak at 6-6 is close to a coin flip adding variance on fast courts.

stages.name: Set-index calibration
stages.description: Win probabilities differ by set number, not only by prior result: the first set carries the settling-in effect (pace of the court, nerves) and the final set carries physical cost and the tiebreak rule. The same pair edge therefore produces a different set-win probability in set 1, set 2 and a decider.
stages.distribution: Systematic shift by set index (illustratively 1-4 points of win probability; unsourced and to be estimated, not assumed); larger for older players and long events.

stages.name: Dependence between consecutive sets
stages.description: Conditional on losing set 1, the probability of winning set 2 falls but usually remains above the base for a favourite; conditional on winning, it rises. Part of this is latent day-level form; part is momentum and tactical change; part is the loser's injury. The size of the link determines the whole spread of the set-count distribution.
stages.distribution: Positive correlation between adjacent set outcomes after controlling for edge (an assumed 0.1-0.3 is unsourced and not identified from set scores alone, see es_dependence_estimation); heavier for bo5.

stages.name: Aggregation to named-set and any-set outcomes
stages.description: The sequence of set results is then summed to the quantities settled: the named set's winner, or at least one set won (any set). These are path-counting transforms: 'any set' is one minus the opponent's straight-sets probability, and a named later set needs the path that makes it exist.
stages.distribution: Discrete distributions over 2-3 (bo3) or 3-5 (bo5) sets; tail probabilities such as 5 sets are sensitive to dependence.

stages.name: Interruption and unplayed-set handling
stages.description: A retirement or walkover can end the match during a set, leaving an unplayed or unfinished set; the settlement outcome of the named set or the any-set contract then depends on the unobserved clause. Pre-match signals of a physical problem precede most such interruptions.
stages.distribution: Rare absorbing event with timing concentrated in the first two sets; heavier tail in bo5.

variants_and_edge_cases: Set that may not be played: 'set 3' in a best-of-three exists only if the match is 1-1, so a set-3 winner contract is conditional on a decider; the sampled text does not say whether an unplayed set resolves No or to a fair price (CONTRACT_AMBIGUOUS).

Any-set wording: KXATPANYSET is title-only, so whether 'any set' means the named player wins at least one set, or any set reaches a named state, and how a retirement before the player wins a set is treated, are not visible.

total_games_and_sets.label: Total games and total sets
total_games_and_sets.target: Total games or sets in the match relative to a strike.
total_games_and_sets.mechanism: Totals derive from the full match distribution: the rating gap (closeness) controls whether it goes the distance, hold probabilities control games per set and tiebreaks, format caps length, and retirement truncates totals. The rung ladder must be consistent with the match-winner and set-spread markets.

inputs.why: Total games per set is driven by hold probabilities: two big servers hold often, push sets to 6-6 and raise totals, two weak servers trade breaks and shorten sets less predictably.
A large rating gap means more 6-2/6-1 sets and fewer games; a closeness measure from the surface rating gap is the main driver of the total ladder relative to the line.
Best-of-five adds up to two sets and a larger total mechanically; the strike level should be read against the format's maximum and median game counts.
A final-set tiebreak versus advantage set changes the right tail of total games enormously (an advantage set can run to 20+ games), so it must match the event's rules.
Each set that reaches 6-6 adds at least one game and often lifts the total over a strike; the probability depends on both players' hold rates.
Some players produce bagels and breadsticks often; a high lopsided-set rate pulls totals under and is partly independent of the average rating gap.
Courts at a given event play consistently fast or slow; the event's past hold percentage is a stronger predictor of games per set than the generic surface label.
A retirement truncates a match and usually settles totals as under or void; the base rate (higher in best-of-five and for injured players) sets how much under-risk the over carries.
Whether a retired match counts games played, voids, or settles on a minimum set count changes the value of the over side.
Totals are listed at several strikes at once; the ladder must be monotonic in probability, so crossed or flat rungs flag stale quotes rather than information.
Serve and return point rates by surface feed the game-level Markov model that generates the distribution of games per set.

mechanism_review.summary: Total games is a sum of games across sets, and it is controlled by two things that move in opposite directions: how many sets are played, and how many games each set takes. A mismatched pair produces short sets (6-1, 6-2) and few sets, so totals fall; an evenly matched pair of big servers produces tiebreak sets (13 games) and decider sets, so totals rise. Hold levels set the games-per-set distribution through a discrete mixture of set scores (6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 12, 13 games), while closeness sets the set count, and format caps both. The two are correlated: a match that goes the distance does so because the sets were close, which also lengthens each set, so the joint distribution is heavier-tailed than a product. The contract adds a truncation layer where completed games before retirement are counted, so the over side can settle early and the under side cannot.

stages.name: Games per set from the two hold rates

contract_review.settlement_definition: The three live games-total series settle on a single number: 'If the number of completed games in the full match is above 28.5 ... then the market resolves to Yes' (strike_type greater, floor_strike at a half point, so no push). The count is every completed game in every set of the match, where counting a tiebreak as one game (a 7-6 set contributing 13) and counting a deciding set's own games are conventions not stated in the sampled text, and an interrupted game at retirement is read as not 'completed' only because the rule says 'completed games'. Non-occurrence before the first ball resolves to a fair price, postponements stay open up to two weeks, and the retirement sentence in the sample says only that markets that can be unconditionally settled from completed play settle on it (cut off). Total sets (KXATPTOTALSETS, now filed here): 'If above 4.5 sets are played' (strike greater, floor 4.5), so in best-of-five it is the five-set event and the bo3 analogue would be 2.5; a fifth set begun and then cut by retirement is presumably 'played' but this is not stated. Whether a 10-point match tiebreak that replaces a third set counts as one game or ten points is not stated.
contract_review.settlement_data_source: Governing-league recorded set scores summed to completed games; the sampled rules text does not name a vendor or a webpage.
variants_and_edge_cases: Retirement asymmetry: the 'over' side can be settled Yes if the completed games already exceed the strike when a player retires, whereas the 'under' side cannot be settled until the match completes; a retirement therefore favours rungs that were already crossed (the retirement sentence in the sample is cut off, so this is inferred).

Assumption not stated in the sampled text (tg_match_tiebreak): a tiebreak counts as one game so a 7-6 set contributes 13 games, and a deciding-set 10-point tiebreak at 6-6 would contribute the same; an advantage deciding set can produce 20+ games and has no cap.

Strikes in this archetype sit at very different levels (26.5 WTA, 28.5 and 32.5 ATP); the rung is only meaningful relative to the match's format (best-of-three versus best-of-five) which is not part of the strike.

Total sets (KXATPTOTALSETS) is now filed here: 'over 4.5 sets' in best-of-five is exactly the 2-2 path, driven by ten.set_count_distribution_by_edge and ten.within_match_dependence; a retirement at 2-1 or during set 4 is not covered by the visible text, and a set that started but was not completed may or may not count as played.

mechanism_review.summary: The exact set score is the match winner combined with a count of how many sets the loser took, so it is a distribution over the paths of a short race rather than a single probability. Each set outcome depends on the pair's point-level serve and return strengths, on who serves first in that set, and on whether the set reaches a tiebreak. The sets are not independent: a latent day-level form shock and in-match physical state push the same player to win consecutive sets, which fattens 2-0 and 3-0 mass relative to independent sets, while a rallying underdog's stamina or an opponent's late-set fade pushes mass into deciders. The favourite's 2-0 frequency also depends on the quality of the tail, not just the mean, because 2-1 and 2-0 for the same player differ only in whether the underdog snatches one set, which is the tail event of the first set. The contract itself adds a truncation layer: a retirement can decide some rungs but not others, so the settlement rule decides which rungs carry retirement risk.

stages.name: Format and rung inventory
stages.description: Before probabilities exist, the format fixes which scorelines are possible: best-of-three gives four outcomes, best-of-five gives six, doubles with a match tiebreak give a different set structure. The deciding-set rule at 6-6 (tiebreak versus advantage) changes how long a deciding set can last but not the set tally, so format mostly acts by fixing the rung grid and the number of sets in which dependence can compound.

stages.name: Set-one win probability for each player
stages.description: The first set is the cleanest read of the pair edge because no in-match history has accrued. The probability that A wins set 1 follows from A's and B's serve-point and return-point strengths and the chance that the set goes to a tiebreak. It is flatter than the match-win probability: a 75% match favourite may be only 62-65% to win the first set.

stages.name: First-server sequence and serve-order advantage
stages.description: Who serves first in each set is deterministic given the starting server and the parity of games in prior sets, and a tiebreak resets the order. Serving first matters more when hold rates are high: a big server who serves first is a few points more likely to win the set, and the advantage rotates across sets so that sets one and three share the same first server in an even-game match but not after a tiebreak.
stages.distribution: Discrete deterministic assignment with a small probability shift (roughly 1-5 points of set-win probability) that scales with the server's hold rate.

stages.name: Between-set dependence and state transitions
stages.description: The probability of winning set 2 depends on who won set 1. Part of this is latent: a player who plays well on the day plays well in both sets. Part is real in-match change: tactics adjustment by the loser, physical fade, momentum. The result is a 2x2 (or bo5 tree) of conditional set-win probabilities that cannot be reconstructed from the match-winner price alone.
stages.distribution: Positive correlation between set outcomes; the conditional probability for the favourite who loses set 1 usually stays above 50% but falls by several points; distribution is bimodal across player types.

stages.name: Length of match and decider incidence
stages.description: Whether the match reaches a deciding set depends on closeness of the pair and on expected length. Long sets, tiebreaks and slow courts raise the probability of 2-1 and 3-2 scorelines for either player while a very lopsided pair converts mass to 2-0 or 3-0. The expected number of service games sets the probability mass of tiebreaks in each set.
stages.distribution: Counts of sets with a heavy mass at the minimum; the decider probability is a smooth convex function of how even the pair is.

stages.name: Retirement truncation and which rungs it settles
stages.description: If a player retires, completed sets fix some rungs as No while others stay unsettled, and the rest of the retirement clause governs them. The share of mass carried by retirement is small but concentrated in the trailing or injured player's rung and in the early-set cases where the unconditional rule helps least.
stages.distribution: Rare absorbing event with timing: more likely just after set 1 or in the middle of set 2; asymmetric between the leader and the trailer.

Match-level tiebreak probability is one minus the product of set non-tiebreak probabilities, so extra sets add less than linearly with positive dependence and exposure saturates for high p.
Straight-set probability is near 25% for even pairs in best-of-three and rises toward the favourite's win probability for large gaps; the middle range is steepest.

mechanism_review.summary: A tiebreak occurs in a set when it reaches six-all, i.e. each player wins six of the first twelve games without either leading by two at 6-x; ten holds is the modal path but alternating breaks also get there. Its probability is a very steep, convex function of the two hold probabilities: at equal holds of 0.80 about 22% of sets reach 6-6, at 0.90 about 38%. A match-level event is then the union over the sets that are played, and the number of sets itself rises with closeness, which is also what produces tiebreaks, so the events are positively dependent across sets and with match length. Because the hold probabilities on the day are uncertain, the convexity means the expected tiebreak probability exceeds the tiebreak probability computed at the expected hold. Straight-set matches are the main suppressor of exposure: the favourite sweeping removes the sets in which a tiebreak could occur, which happens when the edge is large and the sets are positively correlated through a day-level form shock. A retirement and format layer sits on top: a tiebreak that has already occurred locks the contract.

stages.name: Serve hold levels for both players
stages.description: Everything starts with how often each player holds serve against the other. A tiebreak requires the set to reach 6-6, which happens whenever each player wins six of the first twelve games without leading by two earlier; ten holds is the modal path but four or more alternating breaks also reach 6-6, while a hold gap produces straight-set matches with fewer sets; the same two hold probabilities therefore act on the tiebreak event twice, through the per-set 6-6 chance and through the number of sets.
stages.distribution: Two rates in the 0.6-0.92 range; the sum of holds drives tiebreak odds and the difference drives sweep odds.

stages.name: Per-set probability of reaching six-all
stages.description: With holds computed, the probability of 6-6 follows from a dynamic program over the games of the set. It is strongly convex in hold: 0.18 at 0.75, 0.22 at 0.80, 0.28 at 0.85, 0.38 at 0.90. Uncertainty about the day's hold level therefore increases expected tiebreak mass relative to the point estimate.
stages.distribution: Bernoulli per set with probability rising steeply and convexly with hold level; Jensen gap of about two to three points of probability from hold uncertainty.

stages.name: Exposure across sets and format
stages.description: The match-level tiebreak event is a union across the sets played, so the number of sets is an exposure variable: more sets means more chances. Best-of-five and close matches both raise exposure; a deciding set that uses a tiebreak at 6-6 adds an extra exposure with its own rule.
stages.distribution: Union of dependent Bernoulli events across 2-5 sets; exposure itself is random and positively correlated with the event.

stages.name: Dependence across sets and clustering of serving form
stages.description: A player with a hot serving day holds throughout, making tiebreaks in consecutive sets more likely together; the same shock widens the gap and shortens the match. The dependence means the probability of at least one tiebreak is below the independent union but the probability of two or more is above the independent product.
stages.distribution: Positive correlation between sets; overdispersed tiebreak counts relative to a Binomial with a constant p.

stages.name: Straight-set matches as the suppressor of tiebreak exposure
stages.description: The number of sets in which a tiebreak can occur is two or three in best-of-three and three to five in best-of-five, and the minimum is reached when the favourite wins in straight sets. A heavy favourite therefore lowers the match-level tiebreak probability twice: through a lower per-set 6-6 probability and through fewer sets. The straight-set probability depends on the edge, on player-specific set-drop tendencies beyond rating and on whether a tiebreak lottery intervenes, which makes the set-count and tiebreak events jointly determined rather than separable.
stages.distribution: Set count is a discrete mixture (2/3 or 3/4/5) whose straight-set mass rises steeply with edge; the joint tiebreak/set-count table is non-separable.

stages.name: Truncation and settlement
stages.description: A retirement ends the match: a tiebreak already played settles the occurs-contract Yes early under the sibling series' unconditional-settlement clause, while a retirement before any tiebreak leaves the No side to the unseen remainder of that clause. Truncation is small in probability but one-sided: it can only remove future tiebreak exposure, and it is more likely for players with a pre-match physical problem. KXATPTIEBREAK's own text is not available.
stages.distribution: Rare absorbing event; it can only remove future tiebreak exposure, so for the occurs contract it is one-sided (an already-played tiebreak locks Yes).

contract_review.settlement_definition: After the reconciliation one series is filed here: KXATPTIEBREAK ('Tiebreak to occur in Match'), title only with no rules text recovered. A tiebreak-occurs contract would settle Yes if at least one set of the named match reaches a tiebreak; whether a deciding-set 10-point tiebreak counts, how a retirement before any tiebreak is treated, and the source are not visible. The tournament sweep series KXATPSETSWEEP has moved to tournament_winner_futures. Sibling match series that do have rules (totals, spreads, set winners) settle a match that never starts at a fair price and on retirement settle only markets decided by completed play; applying that to KXATPTIEBREAK is an inference.
contract_review.settlement_data_source: Not stated; presumably governing-league recorded set scores with the tiebreak marked in the score string.
variants_and_edge_cases: Tiebreak scope: does the contract count a deciding-set 10-point match tiebreak or only the 7-point tiebreak after a 6-6 set; does a tiebreak in a retired match that already happened settle Yes at once (an early settlement the clause for 'unconditionally settled' markets would allow).
Format dependence: a best-of-five gives five chances for a tiebreak and four sets that can be dropped, while WTA best-of-three gives half as many exposures.

Retirement: a tiebreak that already occurred locks Yes under the sibling series' 'unconditionally settled' clause; with no tiebreak yet, the unsettled side depends on the cut-off remainder of that clause (inferred, no KXATPTIEBREAK text).
Straight-set matches cap exposure: a 2-0 or 3-0 match offers the minimum number of sets for a tiebreak, so the favourite's sweep probability enters this contract only as a suppressor of exposure.

Game win probability is a steep function of spw at deuce and break-point scores, so a given posterior error costs more at 30-30 than at 40-0; the value of better spw information is concentrated in the tight scores.
interactions.how_to_test: Evaluate log loss of the game outcome by score state under alternative prior weights k and compare the benefit by state.

interactions.hypothesis: Ball freshness boosts big servers more than baseliners, so the new-ball uplift in hold probability is a multiple of the server's pace advantage and absent for weak servers.
interactions.how_to_test: Interact the new-ball flag with server ace rate in a hold regression on point-by-point games.

interactions.hypothesis: Wind on one end lowers first-serve in-percentage there and makes second serves the key point; the effect appears only in games served into the wind and flips at changeovers.

interactions.hypothesis: A medical timeout makes past points less representative of future serving, so the posterior should forget faster than the base update rule; ignoring the break underprices the receiver's break chance.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare game outcomes after a trainer visit with predictions from slow-forgetting versus fast-forgetting posterior variants.

interactions.hypothesis: If a game is cut short by retirement or suspension, the traded event settles differently depending on the point score reached: at 40-0 a rule that credits unconditionally decidable results behaves unlike a rule that voids an incomplete game. The settlement regime therefore switches the effective probability by score state, and matters most at the high-leverage deuce and break-point scores.
interactions.how_to_test: Tabulate historical interrupted games by point score at interruption and apply each candidate settlement rule to compute the traded-event probability; compare the spread between rules by score state.

nonlinearities.why: The closed-form game win probability moves from about 0.74 at spw 0.60 to 0.90 at 0.70, so equal posterior errors cost more in the 0.60-0.68 band than outside it.

nonlinearities.shape: piecewise function of the point score
nonlinearities.why: Leverage differs by score: at 40-0 the server's hold probability is near 0.99 and nearly flat in spw, whereas at deuce it is almost the full S-curve.
When first-serve percentage drops below roughly 50% the server is forced onto second serves, and spw falls faster than linearly in the first-serve rate.

mechanism_review.summary: A single tennis game is a race to four points with a two-point margin, and the server wins each point with a probability that is stable enough within a game to be treated as an independent trial. That makes the game outcome a closed-form function of one number, the server's current point-win probability against this returner, and of the point score at the time of trading. The hold probability is steeply nonlinear in that number: it moves from about 0.74 at 0.60 to 0.90 at 0.70. The real mechanism sits one level up: the probability is not the pregame average but a running posterior that is updated by each point already played in the match, shifted by ball age, first-serve percentage drift, wind, an emerging injury, and the pressure of the score. Because the market is traded while play continues, a second layer matters: the score feed that Kalshi settles on and the feed that traders see are not the same clock. The recovered rules add an existence layer: each contract names game N of set M before that game is necessarily reached, so the traded probability is P(set M is played and reaches game N) times P(named player wins that game | reached), and the identity of the server in game N follows deterministically from the first-server sequence and the score path.

stages.name: Pregame serve-point prior for the server in this pair
stages.description: Before any point is played the model needs a prior spw for the server against this returner on this court. It comes from each player's serve quality, the returner's return quality and the court pace, with an uncertainty that is large enough that a one-point error in spw changes the hold chance by about three points at the margin where deuce games are decided.
stages.distribution: Beta-like distribution around 0.58-0.72 on tour; the prior has an effective sample size of a few hundred points rather than a point estimate.

stages.name: In-match posterior update of spw
stages.description: Every point already played in the match updates the server's spw. A beta-binomial update with a prior strength of roughly 40-80 points, adjusted for the first-serve in-percentage drift observed so far, gives a running estimate that departs from the pregame prior when a player is serving unusually well or badly, with the update giving less weight to a few points than to a full set.
stages.distribution: Posterior of a binomial rate: variance shrinks like 1/n of points played; the prior weight, not the data, dominates in the first few games.

stages.name: Game state transition at point level
stages.description: The game is a Markov chain on the point score: 0-0, 15-0, ... deuce, advantage. The win probability at each score is a deterministic function of spw; at 30-30 or deuce the leverage is highest and a probability error costs the most. Break points are pressure points where small differences in the server's first-serve rate matter more than their average.
stages.distribution: Absorbing chain with an infinite-tail deuce loop; discrete scores with sharply non-uniform leverage.

stages.name: Court, ball and weather modifiers during play
stages.description: Wind direction switches at changeovers, at many events new balls are introduced after the first seven games and then every nine (the schedule differs by event and is unverified here), and the sun or roof state can change during the match. These modify spw in a game-specific way that is partially knowable from the order of serving, and which the pregame prior ignores.
stages.distribution: Small systematic shifts of roughly 1-3 points of spw with game-parity structure rather than random noise.

stages.name: Physical deterioration and in-match health
stages.description: Medical timeouts, visible movement problems, drops in first-serve speed and increased double faults are signs the server's spw will fall during the match. The signal arrives through the live feed and television rather than any pre-match source and is binary-like in its effect: a trained trainer visit lowers the hold probability by several points for the rest of the match.
stages.distribution: Regime change with a small probability but a large shift in the serve rate; positively skewed risk of a worse spw.

stages.name: Settlement rule and interrupted-game handling
stages.description: The market resolves on the official result of the named game. The recovered text settles a match that never starts at a fair price, keeps a postponed match open up to two weeks, and on retirement settles only markets that can be unconditionally settled from play already completed (the game-winner samples are cut off at 'based on p'); the remainder of that clause is not visible, so a retirement before or inside the named game, a named game that is never reached, a game decided by point or code penalty and a tiebreak counted as game 13 remain unread. Feed timing is excluded from this stage on purpose: it affects when a trader can act, not who wins the game.
stages.distribution: Rare discrete regime: P(interruption) per game is very small and concentrated at high-leverage scores; otherwise the outcome is the Bernoulli chain of stage s3.

stages.name: Existence of the named game and identity of its server
stages.description: The rules name game N of set M (S1-S5 series) for one player. Before that game starts the contract carries two extra uncertainties: whether the match reaches set M (a set-3 market needs 1-1 in best-of-three, set 4/5 markets need best-of-five) and whether set M lasts N games (game 10 needs both players to have at least four games, so a 6-3 set never reaches it; game 13 exists only at 6-6). Given existence, game N is served by the player who served first in set M if N is odd, otherwise by the other, so the event is a hold for one player and a break for the other; the first server of set M depends on the toss and on the parity of games in previous sets.
stages.distribution: Bernoulli existence mass from the games-per-set and set-count distributions (discrete, heavily dependent on the hold gap) times a hold or break probability; parity creates a two-point mixture before the server of set M is known.

role_personnel.note: A game is played by two fixed singles players with no lineup or substitution; roles are limited to who serves, covered by server_game_state, not a personnel question.

coaching_scheme.note: Coaching during a game is limited by rule and there is no observable tactical variable at game-resolution scale; any strategic shift appears in the point-win statistics.

pace_volume.note: Within a game there is no volume driver, but the contract's existence depends on how many games set M lasts and whether set M is played (stage s7), which these distributions supply.

situational_schedule_motivation.note: Rest and schedule effects enter through the pre-match spw prior and are far smaller than in-match information; no separate game-level schedule variable is identifiable.

contract_review.settlement_definition: Six series are filed here: KXATPS1GWINNER, KXATPS2GWINNER, KXATPS3GWINNER, KXATPS4GWINNER (rules text recovered from archived markets), KXATPS5GWINNER and KXATPGWINNER (title only). Each market is a binary on one named player winning one numbered game of one numbered set: 'If Sho Shimabukuro wins game 10 in set 1 in the ... match ..., then the market resolves to Yes'. The set number is fixed by the series (S1..S5) and the game number by the market, so whether the named player is serving (a hold) or receiving (a break) follows from the first-server sequence and is not stated. If the match never starts (injury, walkover, forfeiture, cancellation before the first ball) the market resolves to a fair price; a postponed match stays open until the rescheduled match finishes (within two weeks). On retirement, 'all markets that can be unconditionally settled base[d on p...]' settle on completed play; the game-winner samples are cut off at 'based on p', so the rest of the clause is not visible. The text is silent on a named game that is never reached (set ends before game N, or set 4/5 not played), on whether game 13 (the tiebreak) counts as a game, and on the source of truth.
contract_review.settlement_data_source: Not named in the sampled rules; presumably the governing league's official score (ATP/Challenger live scoring). UNVERIFIED.
variants_and_edge_cases: Hold versus break: the named game's server is determined by who served first in the set (toss for set 1, game parity and tiebreak rule for later sets), so 'player X wins game 10' is a hold for one player and a break for the other; the rule text does not say which.
Unreached game: a set that ends 6-2 has eight games, so a game-10 market may never be played; the sampled rules do not say whether it resolves No, at a fair price or is cancelled (gw_no_rules).
Game 13 of a set is a tiebreak recorded as one game in the score; whether a tiebreak counts as 'game 13' for these markets is not stated.

Set existence: S3 markets need a third set and S4/S5 markets need four or five sets. All four sampled matches are best-of-three qualifying matches, yet KXATPS4GWINNER lists game 6 of set 4 in a 's-Hertogenbosch qualifier where a fourth set cannot exist; how such a structurally unreachable market settles is not stated (gw_no_rules), so set existence must be read from the event format, not assumed from the series.

Retirement: completed games settle; a retirement inside or before the named game falls into the cut-off part of the clause. Listing time (pregame versus during play) is not visible, so whether existence risk is priced in is unknown.
KXATPGWINNER and KXATPS5GWINNER are title only; they are assumed to share the S1-S4 wording.

player_aces_and_double_faults.mechanism: Counts equal rates times opportunities: ace rate per service point (server ability, returner ability, surface, altitude, wind) times expected service points (closeness and format), with overdispersion from day-level first-serve variation. The official stats source and retirement rules define what counts.
