interactions.hypothesis: Counts scale with both rate and length, so favourites in short matches get fewer expected aces.
Altitude amplifies big servers' ace rate.
Wind raises count variance through in%.

Expected aces equal rate times service points, but the two are negatively correlated: a server with a high ace rate holds quickly, uses fewer points per game and wins faster, so the product is lower than the naive product for big servers.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare realised ace counts with rate times exposure computed with and without conditioning on match scenario for high-ace-rate servers.

interactions.hypothesis: Thin air reduces drag so the ball carries pace; players with high serve speed gain more in absolute ace probability than slower servers.
interactions.how_to_test: Regress ace rate on altitude interacted with serve speed percentile.

interactions.hypothesis: Wind lowers first-serve in-percentage on the windward end, which reduces aces there and raises double faults; the effect shows up as extra variance, not a mean shift.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare variance of ace counts across outdoor wind bins and indoor matches.

interactions.hypothesis: A drop in first-serve speed over the last matches signals fatigue or an arm problem; a hurt server tends to protect the first serve (fewer aces) while the safer second serve may or may not keep the double-fault rate down, so the sign of the double-fault response depends on how the player adapts. The link is conditional on a speed-drop regime, not additive.
interactions.how_to_test: Split player-matches by the first-serve speed z-score (below -1 versus above) and compare ace rate and double-fault rate per service point, conditioning on opponent return aggression; test whether the double-fault slope differs by regime.

interactions.hypothesis: Raising first-serve pace raises ace given in but lowers in-percentage and adds second-serve points where double faults occur; aces and double faults move together with a non-monotone net effect.
interactions.how_to_test: Plot aces and double faults per service point against first-serve in% across player-matches and check for an interior optimum.

nonlinearities.shape: concave trade-off between in-percentage and ace probability
nonlinearities.why: Ace probability given a first serve in rises with pace while in-percentage falls, so aces per service point has an interior maximum rather than increasing with pace.
A match that goes to a fifth set adds 25-40 service points for each player, so exposure is bimodal in best-of-five and the count distribution inherits a heavy right tail.
Ace probability rises with altitude but flattens beyond moderate elevations because court and ball conditions dominate once the air is thin.

mechanism_review.summary: An ace count is the number of service points on which a given server is not touched by the returner, so it is a sum over the points he serves of a rare event whose per-point probability depends on the server's pace and placement, the returner's reach and position, the court and the air. The count is therefore rate times exposure. Exposure is the number of service points the player serves, which depends on the number of games played, on how long each service game lasts (quick holds use fewer points than deuce-heavy ones) and on whether tiebreaks are played, and it is endogenous: a big server who holds quickly serves fewer points per game. The rate is the product of first-serve in-percentage and ace probability given first-serve in, plus small second-serve ace and double-fault terms, and varies from day to day beyond binomial noise because first-serve percentage and serve speed move together with form and conditions. Double faults mirror this through second-serve policy and pressure. The settlement layer is the official count and its truncation at retirement.

stages.name: Expected service points as the exposure
stages.description: Every ace needs a service point, so the first object is the number of points the named player serves. It is the number of service games times points per game, plus the player's share of tiebreak points. Points per game is not constant: a game held to love takes four points, a deuce game six or more, so the average depends on the spw and the returner.
stages.distribution: Discrete exposure around 60-110 service points in a best-of-three and roughly 90-180 in a best-of-five (the sampled KXATPACES market is a Wimbledon men's match, so best-of-five); mixture over match scenarios (straight-set win, loss, three sets, tiebreaks) with a heavy right tail from long matches.

stages.name: First-serve in-rate and ace probability given first serve in
stages.description: The per-point ace probability is the product of the share of first serves that land in and the probability that a first serve in is untouched. A player who takes pace off to land more first serves lowers the ace chance given in; a player who hits for pace raises both ace probability and fault risk, so the trade-off is non-monotone.
stages.distribution: Two linked Bernoulli rates (illustrative ranges, to be estimated from data rather than taken as established: in% roughly 0.55-0.70, ace given in a few percent to about a third for elite servers); product has a limited range with a negative trade-off between the two components.

stages.name: Returner and direction effects
stages.description: Aces depend on the returner: reach, return position, handedness and tendency to stand deep. A tall left-handed server using the wide serve on the ad court against a weak backhand return produces more aces than the average. The pair interaction is strong because the ace is the returner's failure to touch the ball.
stages.distribution: Rate varies by factor 2 across returners for the same server; interaction with serve direction mix.

stages.name: Court, air and condition shifts
stages.description: Fast courts, high altitude (thin air reduces drag), indoor stillness and the ball in use all raise ace probability; wind adds variance and side-dependent effects. These are event-level shifts that apply to every match at that event and week, so the event's own history of ace rates is the best predictor.
stages.distribution: Event-level location shifts of 10-40% in ace rate; wind is additional noise with side asymmetry.

stages.name: Day-level variation, double-fault pressure and overdispersion
stages.description: Ace counts are more variable than a binomial: a day with a hot first serve yields many more. Double faults come from second-serve risk and pressure at critical points; both counts share the day-level first-serve factor, producing overdispersion relative to a constant-rate count.
stages.distribution: Overdispersed count (negative-binomial or beta-binomial) with a variance-to-mean ratio above one that is a parameter to estimate (an assumed 1.5-3 is unsourced); zero-inflation small.

stages.name: Counting rule and truncation
stages.description: The settled count is whatever the official statistics record: KXATPACES defines an ace as an untouched legal serve and resolves on 'statistics officially completed and recorded'. Let-cord serves, challenged calls and foot faults can shift the recorded number by one or two, and a retirement stops the count at that moment and settles every rung on it, so unreached rungs lose. These rules matter most for ladder rungs close to the median and for players with a high retirement hazard.
stages.distribution: Rare discrete discrepancies of 0-2 aces between sources; truncation concentrates in retiring or injured players.

situational_schedule_motivation.note: Rest and schedule shift serve speed by small amounts relative to the exposure and the opponent effects; no standalone variable is justified at the match level.

contract_review.settlement_definition: One live series, KXATPACES, with recovered rules: 'If Taylor Fritz records at least 19 total match aces in the full match of the ... match ..., then the market resolves to Yes' (floor_strike 18.5, so each market is an 'N+' rung on one player's full-match ace count). An ace is defined as 'A serve that lands in the service box and is not touched by the receiving player ... resulting in an immediate point for the server'. A match that never starts resolves to a fair price. On retirement 'all markets will resolve based on the statistics officially completed and recorded prior to the cancellation or discontinuation of the match', so the count is truncated and unreached rungs settle No rather than void. No double-fault series is listed. The text does not name the statistics provider, does not contain the postponement sentence used by the game-level series, and is silent on whether tiebreak and match-tiebreak serves count (they are serves, so presumably yes).
contract_review.settlement_data_source: 'Statistics officially completed and recorded' (provider not named); presumably the ATP/Slam official match statistics.
variants_and_edge_cases: Strike construction: 'at least N' rungs from one player's count (19+ sampled); rungs are nested, so their probabilities must be monotone in N.
Retirement: truncation at the officially recorded count; a retirement by either player ends the server's exposure, so the opponent's retirement hazard also lowers the named player's over probability.

Source of truth: 'statistics officially completed and recorded' without a named provider; official ATP statistics and broadcaster or vendor counts can differ by one or two aces (ac_source_disagreement).
Postponement: unlike the game-level series, the sampled ace text has no postponement sentence; whether a suspended match continuing the next day is still the same market is not stated.

Double faults and match totals: no double-fault or match-total ace series is listed, so stage s5 (double-fault pressure) and the pair-correlation gap are conditional on such a series being listed; they stay as mechanism content for the shared first-serve factor.

tournament_winner_futures.mechanism: Futures are a path product of match-win probabilities across a specific bracket, with fatigue accumulation, seeding, withdrawals and correlation within halves. nonlinearities.why: Title probability is a product of round-by-round probabilities, so a one-point change in per-match win probability has a larger relative effect on the title for a longer path than a shorter one.

mechanism_review.summary: A tournament outcome is a path product across a bracket: to win, a player must be in the field, avoid injury, and win about six or seven consecutive matches against opponents determined by a draw that is random subject to seeding. Before the draw is published the probability averages over draw randomness, flattening the favourite; after the draw it is conditional on the actual path. Within an event the path is not independent across rounds, since fatigue accumulates, injuries occur, in-tournament form updates, and withdrawals reshuffle the bracket, and across players in the same half the outcomes are coupled because one player's win removes another's path. Round-robin finals and team formats replace the path product with a group structure and tie-break rules. The settlement layer adds a distinct feature: for stage contracts a player who qualifies but does not play the final still pays, so withdrawal timing matters differently by stage.

stages.name: Field formation: entry, withdrawals and replacement
stages.description: The field is determined by entry lists, withdrawals before and after the draw, and replacement by alternates and lucky losers. A top player's absence removes the main competitor for everyone else and changes the bracket. Withdrawals concentrate among players with injury layoffs and are timestamped in a way that matters to price.
stages.distribution: Discrete field composition with a withdrawal hazard concentrated close to the draw and first match; clustered in injured and older players.

stages.name: Draw structure and seeding
stages.description: Seeding rules separate the top seeds into different quarters, so a seed's expected opponent strength in early rounds is determined by those rules. Before the draw the model averages over random placement conditional on seeding; after it, the actual bracket sets each player's path difficulty and potential meetings. Round-robin finals replace this with group composition.
stages.distribution: Combinatorial distribution of brackets under seeding constraints; heterogeneity in path difficulty is large for players seeded 5-8.

stages.name: Match-level win probabilities with uncertainty
stages.description: Each match on the path has a win probability from surface-adjusted ratings at the event's pace, with honest uncertainty. Rating uncertainty flattens favourites and matters because a title is the product of six or seven probabilities, so small per-match errors compound.
stages.distribution: Product of 6-7 Bernoulli probabilities; relative error of the product is about the sum of relative errors per match.

stages.name: Path dependence: fatigue, in-event updating and injury
stages.description: Long early matches cost later performance, and in-event results update the ratings (a player playing at a high level through four rounds is more likely to continue). Qualifiers and lucky losers carry a different load profile. Injury risk accumulates across rounds and in best-of-five formats.
stages.distribution: Positively correlated successive match outcomes; fatigue effects are small per round but compound over seven rounds.

stages.name: Dependence within the draw and nationality coupling
stages.description: Players in the same half cannot both reach the final, so their outcomes are negatively dependent; upset shocks shared across top seeds create positive dependence among their early losses. For the stage contracts (KXATPADVANCE/KXWTAADVANCE) two players in the same half are mutually exclusive finalists, and for KXWTAROE one player's elimination round fixes the opponent's next round.
stages.distribution: Joint distribution with negative dependence within halves and positive dependence in shared shocks; covariance depends on bracket positions.

stages.name: Settlement of outright and stage contracts
stages.description: Outright-winner contracts settle No for a participant who withdraws or is removed, while stage contracts settle Yes once the player qualifies for the Final even if he does not compete; the same withdrawal therefore has opposite payoffs by contract type. For season-finals winner contracts listed before the field is set, the remaining race decides who is in the field, so race arithmetic enters only as field formation context. Round-winner series settle on winning the named round (the title when the round is the final), and KXWTAROE needs the full PMF of the elimination round, P(reach r) - P(reach r+1), with a withdrawal after a win assigned to the next round, so in-event withdrawal hazard shifts mass one round later instead of to No.
stages.distribution: Point mass on settlement at qualification or withdrawal events; a Bernoulli withdrawal hazard whose payoff sign depends on contract type.

stages.name: Tournament set-drop path for the no-dropped-set title
stages.description: KXATPSETSWEEP pays only if the named player wins the title and wins every completed set. Per round this is P(win) times P(straight sets | win) against the round's opponent distribution, and the title-level probability is the product over rounds with a shared form shock that makes clean early rounds predictive of clean later ones. Best-of-five Slams require seven 3-0 wins, so the event is far rarer than the title and concentrated on dominant servers with a low set-drop propensity; walkovers and opponent retirements before a completed set count in the player's favour under the completed-set rule.
stages.distribution: Product of round-level Bernoulli probabilities with positive dependence; heavy concentration at near zero for all but one or two players; extremely sensitive to the straight-set conversion curve at high edges.

stages.name: Return-gated any-event title for inactive players
stages.description: KXWTATOURNWIN asks whether a named player wins any WTA tournament, singles or doubles, within 2026; the sample names a retired player. The probability is P(returns to competition in time) times P(at least one title over the events entered), where the second factor is a union over a short schedule and doubles events offer an easier path (smaller fields, partner choice). For an active player it reduces to a calendar union of title probabilities with health-linked dependence across events.
stages.distribution: Mixture of a point mass at zero (no return) and a union over a few events with small per-event probabilities; positively dependent through form and health; doubles adds a separate path.

coaching_scheme.note: No coaching or tactical variable is observable at tournament-path scale; effects pass through ratings and form, and there is no separate coaching quantity to forecast.

pace_volume.note: A tournament contract has no volume count; the number of rounds is fixed by the draw size and format and is not a forecast quantity.

contract_review.settlement_definition: Seventeen live series; all but KXATPMEN (title only) now have rules text. Outright winners: KXATP and KXWTA ('If Matteo Berrettini wins the 2026 ATP Paris professional tennis tournament') resolve No for a participant who 'forfeits, withdraws from consideration, or takes any official action that removes them from being able to win'; KXATPFINALS, KXWTAFINALS and KXATPNEXTGEN have only a primary sentence. Round-winner series (KXATPIWO, KXATPIT, KXWTAIT, KXATPMCO, KXWTAMOA, KXWTAATX; archived 2025 markets) settle on the player being 'a winner of the final/quarterfinal' of the event, i.e. winning that round (for a final, the title; otherwise equivalent to reaching the next stage). Stage contracts KXATPADVANCE/KXWTAADVANCE settle Yes on qualifying for the Final 'if they qualify but do not end up competing'. KXWTAROE settles on the exact round of elimination, with a withdrawal assigned to the next stage the player would have been eliminated in. KXATPSETSWEEP requires winning the tournament while winning 'every completed set they play'; retirement, walkover, default or disqualification follow official advancement and scoring records. KXWTATOURNWIN settles Yes if the named player wins any WTA tournament, singles or doubles, in 2026. Not stated: lucky-loser replacement, a final decided by walkover for the outright, and the source of truth.
contract_review.settlement_data_source: Official tournament draw and results (final slot reached); for qualification contracts the governing league's published qualification list. Source not named in the sample.
variants_and_edge_cases: Round-robin finals (ATP Finals, WTA Finals, Next Gen Finals): a group stage with qualification to semifinals by wins, then by head-to-head, set ratio and game ratio, plus alternates replacing withdrawn players; the structure differs from a knockout bracket.

Withdrawal asymmetry: outright winners settle No if the participant withdraws (KXATP, KXWTA), stage contracts settle Yes if the player qualified for the Final but does not compete (KXATPADVANCE/KXWTAADVANCE), and KXWTAROE assigns a withdrawing player the next elimination stage; the same withdrawal moves the three contract types differently.

Tournament sweep (KXATPSETSWEEP): Yes needs the title plus every completed set won; an opponent retiring mid-set leaves the unfinished set uncounted, while a walkover adds a round with no sets, so retirements and walkovers raise the sweep probability relative to a full-play model.

Round-winner series (KXATPIWO, KXATPIT, KXWTAIT, KXATPMCO, KXWTAMOA, KXWTAATX) and the identical tournament-named series filed under match_winner (KXATPMAD, KXWTAIWO ...) are the same object; listing time relative to the draw is not stated.

KXWTATOURNWIN names players who may not be active (sample: Serena Williams); for them the event is gated by a return to competition, and doubles titles count, which is a different path from singles strength.
Season finals and Next Gen winner series (KXATPFINALS, KXWTAFINALS, KXATPNEXTGEN) have only a primary sentence; their withdrawal and alternate treatment is not stated.

interactions.hypothesis: A collision between compatriots removes one of them only if both reach the meeting round healthy; an injury or withdrawal of one compatriot before that round converts the would-be collision into a walkover for the other, so the union loss from a collision shrinks as the injury probability of either rises. The effect is largest when two strong compatriots are drawn into the same quarter.

nonlinearities.why: Union probability is one minus the product of failures, so each extra compatriot adds a smaller increment, especially when the top compatriot has a high individual probability.
The dependence appears at the first round where two compatriots can meet; before it the union is close to independent, after it the correction is exact and large.

nonlinearities.why: A best-of-three tie amplifies rubber edges: the tie win probability of the better team rises faster than the rubber win probability for edges above about 55%.

mechanism_review.summary: A nationality contract asks whether any member of a national group achieves an individual outcome, so it is a union over the compatriots in a draw rather than a property of one player. The union is built from each player's individual path probability but is reduced by a structural dependence: two compatriots in the same half of a bracket cannot both reach the final, and every meeting between them removes one candidate with certainty. A count contract adds a threshold on the number of successes, which depends on the number of compatriots, their strengths and the geometry of the draw. Team competitions replace the path product with rubber-level aggregation: a tie is decided by singles and doubles rubbers that depend on who is nominated, which surface the host chooses, and how fatigue and doubles availability play out, followed by group or knockout advancement rules. The two settings share a settlement dependency on how the league designates each player's nationality and on who actually competes.

stages.name: Who counts: roster definition and nationality designation
stages.description: The contract population is the set of players the league designates as the nation's, which can differ from passport or residence: players competing as neutral athletes, switching allegiance or holding dual nationality are settlement edge cases. The roster for a draw also depends on entries and withdrawals before and after the draw.
stages.distribution: Discrete roster of 0-12 compatriots per draw; the designation uncertainty affects a handful of players but can dominate a small national group.

stages.name: Individual probabilities of reaching the stage
stages.description: Each compatriot has an individual probability of winning or reaching a stage, from the path simulation with surface-adjusted ratings, the draw and fatigue. These are marginals; the union cannot be built from them alone.
stages.distribution: Marginals ranging from under 1% for qualifiers to 20-40% for top players; very skewed across the roster with depth beyond the top two mattering little.

stages.name: Compatriot collisions in the bracket
stages.description: If two compatriots can meet before the stage, the meeting removes one with certainty. The probability that both reach the collision round and meet reduces the union probability relative to independence, and the effect depends on draw positions, which are random before the draw and fixed after.
stages.distribution: Pairwise collision probabilities by round, strongly dependent on bracket geometry; mass concentrated in rounds 2-3 for players seeded close together.

stages.name: Union and count aggregation
stages.description: The union probability is built from marginals and collision structure: P(at least one) is one minus the probability that all fail, with positive dependence from shared conditions (court speed, travel) and negative dependence from collisions. Count thresholds use the full distribution of the number of successes.
stages.distribution: Discrete count distribution on 0-2 at the final stage, 0-8 at earlier rounds; union saturates with roster depth.

stages.name: Team-competition rubber model
stages.description: Conditional stage (no team-competition series is listed live; apply only if one is listed). For a team tie, the outcome is the number of rubbers won: nominated singles players, a doubles pair, and the order. Captains choose the lineup, the host selects the surface and court speed, and fatigue across days alters the third rubber. The tie win probability needs the lineup distribution, not just top players' ratings.
stages.distribution: Discrete tie outcomes (2-0, 2-1, 1-2, 0-2) from rubber probabilities that are correlated through the host's surface and the lineup; the deciding doubles has the highest variance.

stages.name: Group advancement and settlement rules
stages.description: Conditional stage (no team-competition series is listed live; apply only if one is listed). Team competitions with a group phase use tie-break orders (ties won, rubbers, sets, games) and nationalities rules for eligibility; these determine advancement in close groups. The motivation of players to attend, and whether the event is an exhibition, adds a participation uncertainty.
stages.distribution: Rule-driven discrete advancement; the probability mass in tie-break resolution is small but decisive in close groups.

pace_volume.note: There is no volume quantity: the outcome is a union or a count of players or rubbers, whose number is fixed by the format rather than forecast as a rate times opportunities.

contract_review.settlement_definition: Three live series are filed here after the reconciliation and all carry rules text. KXATPNATWINNER: 'If an American woman wins the women's singles title in the 2026 US Open tennis tournament, then the market resolves to Yes', with nationalities 'designated by the Governing League' - a union over every compatriot in the named draw. KXATPNATSTAGE ('If 1+ Americans reach the Final in the 2026 US Open Men's Singles', greater_or_equal, floor 1) and KXWTANATSTAGE ('If 3+ Americans reach the Semifinals in the 2026 US Open Women's Singles', floor 3) are counts of compatriots reaching a named round with an N+ threshold; the Final holds at most two players and the semifinals four. None of the sampled texts states how a compatriot who reaches the round and then withdraws, a walkover into the round, or a change of designation is treated, and no source of truth is named. Team-competition contracts (Davis Cup, BJK Cup, United Cup, Laver Cup) are not listed and their rules are unknown. This record owns the union/count aggregation, collision structure and designation rules; tournament_winner_futures supplies the per-player path marginals.
contract_review.settlement_data_source: Governing league's designated nationality for each player and the official tournament or tie results; no vendor named.
variants_and_edge_cases: Nationality designation: KXATPNATWINNER and KXWTANATSTAGE defer to the governing league's designated nationality, so players competing under a neutral designation, with dual nationality or after a switch of allegiance are settlement edge cases not resolved by any text visible here. KXATPNATSTAGE's sampled text has no designation sentence at all.

Union versus count: 'an American wins' is a union over all compatriots in the draw (probability at least one), whereas '2+ Americans reach the Final' is a count with a threshold, and the two have different dependence structure (the Final can hold at most two players).

Walkover and withdrawal: the 'qualify but do not end up competing, still Yes' sentence belongs to KXATPADVANCE/KXWTAADVANCE (tournament_winner_futures), not to the NATSTAGE texts, which only say 'reach the Final/Semifinals'; whether a compatriot who reaches the round and then withdraws, or advances into it by walkover, counts is not stated for any series here, and the title contract has no withdrawal sentence either.

Team events: tie-level results (best of three rubbers, with doubles as the decider), group-stage tie-break order, and a team withdrawing or forfeiting all create edge cases that the nationality-winner text does not cover.

Rules-text status: KXATPNATWINNER, KXATPNATSTAGE and KXWTANATSTAGE are now filed here and their rules are quoted; the count thresholds vary by series (1+ to the Final, 3+ to the Semifinals) so the archetype needs the whole count distribution. Verification is partial because withdrawal-after-reaching-the-round, designation source and source of truth are not stated.

The probability that a trailing player overtakes the leader is zero if the points gap exceeds the maximum remaining swing, and rises steeply once the gap falls inside it; the effect is a threshold, not a smooth function.
interactions.how_to_test: Compute the historical frequency of year-end #1 changes by the ratio of points gap to maximum remaining swing at the start of November.

interactions.how_to_test: Estimate participation and win conditional separately by age bin and compare the product with the unconditional rate.

interactions.hypothesis: The best-of-five premium only applies in majors; a player with high endurance gains most in the later rounds against rivals of similar rating.

nonlinearities.shape: threshold then probit in gap over remaining swing

nonlinearities.shape: accelerating decline in major probability after about 35
nonlinearities.why: Participation, endurance in best-of-five and injury hazard worsen faster than linearly with age, so a linear age effect understates the drop for players above 36.
The probability of at least one title is one minus the product of failures, which saturates for players with moderate per-major probability and compresses differences between contenders.

mechanism_review.summary: These contracts are aggregates over a finite remaining calendar, so the central object is the horizon: what can still change before the settlement date. In early November a year-end ranking is nearly determined by the points already earned and by a small number of remaining events (the final Masters and the Finals; team events such as the Davis Cup finals and Laver Cup award no ATP/WTA ranking points and matter only through whether players skip or play point-bearing events), so the question is whether the remaining maximum swing can overturn the current gap, and the probability moves in a threshold fashion as the lead approaches the size of that swing. A long-horizon major contract is different: it is a union of independent but correlated four-tournament lotteries, in which each player's probability is the chance he is healthy, enters, and wins seven best-of-five matches, concentrated among a handful of players, with a large downside from injury and age. The rules add a snapshot definition (published ranking at a clock time), a singles-only count and a career-cumulative target that depend on state at issuance.

stages.name: Current standing and the remaining points arithmetic
stages.description: The ranking list at settlement equals current 52-week points minus points dropping off plus points earned in the remaining events. Late in the season both sets are known: drop-offs are deterministic by calendar, and the maximum available points are fixed by the event structure (for example the Finals' round-robin plus knockout allocation). This makes the question closer to a race bounded by arithmetic than to a pure forecast. Finals qualification (KXATPFINALSQUAL, KXWTAFINALSQUAL) uses the same arithmetic on the calendar-year Race, which has no drop-offs: the top eight in the Race after the last counting event qualify (ATP: a current-year major champion ranked 9-20 takes the eighth place, outside knowledge), and because 'qualifies but does not compete' still pays Yes, later withdrawal does not lower the qualifier's probability.
stages.distribution: Deterministic bounds plus a residual uncertainty from match outcomes; the probability of overtaking is zero if the gap exceeds the maximum swing.

stages.name: Event participation and health for remaining events
stages.description: Whether a contender plays the remaining events is a gating variable: withdrawals from the Finals, injuries and fatigue after a long season remove points from the maximum. Injury and age raise the probability that a leader skips events, and a skip can reduce the leader's points to fixed levels.
stages.distribution: Binary participation with strong dependence on injury state; the number of events missed has a heavy tail for injured players.

stages.name: Match-level strength in each remaining event
stages.description: Within events that are played, results depend on surface-adjusted strength; for the year-end rank the surface is mostly indoor hard, so the relevant rating is the indoor-hard rating of the contenders, with a strong dependence on the draw and round-robin groups.
stages.distribution: Match-level Bernoulli draws aggregated through event structure; round-robin events give variance structure that differs from knockout.

stages.name: Major-title probability as a union over four events
stages.description: For the 2027 major contracts, each player has a title probability in each major, depending on the draw, surface, best-of-five edge and health. The probability of at least one title is one minus the product of non-title probabilities, with positive correlation through health and form, so concentrated among the top few players. Variants: a one-season window (KXTENNISMAJORDJOKOVIC, 2025) uses the same union over fewer events; the field contract (KXATPGRANDSLAMFIELD) is one minus the product over remaining majors of P(champion is Alcaraz or Sinner), which needs each named player's participation hazard and the per-event champion distribution of the whole field, so the two players' titles are mutually exclusive within an event and positively linked across events only through health.
stages.distribution: Union of four dependent rare events (individual title probabilities 1-40% for contenders, below 2% for most); strong concentration with heavy skew.

stages.name: Age, longevity and the cumulative-count path
stages.description: A career-cumulative contract needs the player to still be competing and healthy: age-related decline in endurance in best-of-five, injury frequency and retirement hazard all lower the chance of one more major, and the count at issuance fixes the target. For veterans the horizon is short and the probability dominated by availability, not skill.
stages.distribution: Survival-times-conversion structure: P(play a major) times P(win | play); right tail small for players over 38.

stages.name: Snapshot and publication rule
stages.description: The rank contract resolves on the most recently published list at a stated clock time; the publication calendar (rankings are published on Mondays, and in the off-season the list may not change) fixes which list applies. Rules on ties, protected points and withdrawals determine the final figure.
stages.distribution: Calendar-determined discrete rule; error concentrates around ties or last-minute publications.

contract_review.settlement_definition: Three settled families. Year-end rank contracts (KXATP1RANK, KXWTA1RANK, KXATPT5RANK) settle on the published rankings: 'If Taylor Fritz is the #1 ranked on the PIF ATP singles rankings on Dec 31, 2026 at 12:00 PM ET', using 'the most recently published PIF ATP Rankings available at the time of resolution', so the settlement is the last published weekly list, not a points total computed on that date. Major-title contracts (KXATPGRANDSLAM, KXWTAGRANDSLAM) settle Yes if the named player 'wins a tennis major (the Australian Open, the French Open, Wimbledon, or the U.S. Open) after Issuance and before Dec 31, 2027', a union over the four majors of 2027 plus any remaining 2026 major at issuance. The cumulative contract (KXATPNOVAK25) requires a named player's 25th career major singles title before 2028 and counts singles only, so it also depends on his current count. No sampled text covers a player's retirement, withdrawal, or disqualification inside a major. Finals-qualification contracts (KXATPFINALSQUAL, KXWTAFINALSQUAL) settle Yes if the named player 'qualifies for the 2026 Nitto ATP Singles Finals' (or WTA Singles Finals), and a qualified player who does not compete still settles Yes; whether a promoted alternate counts as qualified is not stated. Two further major series: KXTENNISMAJORDJOKOVIC ('If Novak Djokovic wins a tennis major ... before Dec 31, 2025') is a one-player union over the 2025 majors (window closed before today's date), and KXATPGRANDSLAMFIELD settles Yes 'If any man other than Carlos Alcaraz and Jannik Sinner wins a tennis major ... before Dec 31, 2026', the complement of the two named players winning every remaining major; neither has secondary text.
contract_review.settlement_data_source: PIF ATP Rankings and PIF WTA Rankings as published by the governing league (rank contracts); official tournament results for major titles.
variants_and_edge_cases: The ranking is the most recently published list, and ATP and WTA weeks without events may not publish; the Dec 31, 2026 12:00 PM ET snapshot is a Thursday, so the settlement list is probably the one issued after the final tournament, not a date-stamped calculation (SOURCE_UNVERIFIED publication calendar).

Window start for the major contracts is 'after Issuance', whose timestamp is not in the sample; a major that finished between issuance and today would count, and the window closes at 'before Dec 31, 2027' so only the 2027 majors remain after today's date (Nov 2026).

Cumulative contract: 'his 25th career major' depends on the count at issuance (a count of 24 at issuance is outside knowledge, not stated in the rules text); a title already won since issuance would shift the target, and retirement or a mid-tournament withdrawal ends the path.

Top-5 contract: a threshold on rank rather than a unique winner, so ties in points are broken by the governing league rules (not visible), and a rank of 5 versus 6 depends on small margins around the cutoff.

Finals qualification (KXATPFINALSQUAL, KXWTAFINALSQUAL, now filed here with rules text): Yes if the named player 'qualifies' for the ATP/WTA singles Finals, and 'If player qualifies but does not compete, the market resolves to Yes'. Not stated: whether an alternate who is promoted after a withdrawal counts as having qualified, the qualification cut-off date, and the ATP rule (outside knowledge, to be checked in the rulebook) that a current-year Grand Slam champion ranked 9-20 in the Race takes the 8th place.

Verification level: rules text was read for all ten series, but Top-5 and #1 tie-break rules, the issuance timestamp (sr_issuance_timestamp), the publication calendar and the alternate/Slam-champion qualification rules are not visible, so the contract is only partially verified.

Field and single-season major contracts (KXATPGRANDSLAMFIELD, KXTENNISMAJORDJOKOVIC): no secondary text, no 'after Issuance' clause and no withdrawal rule; the field contract pays Yes on one non-Alcaraz/Sinner title among the remaining majors, so it depends on the joint champion distribution per event (both named players' participation and the strength of the rest of the field), not on either player's marginal alone. All majors inside both windows (2025; 2026, last major the US Open in September) have been played by November 2026, so these series are effectively decided.

Two surface ratings of the same player are drawn from a correlated joint posterior; high covariance raises the probability of winning both and low covariance behaves like independence, so the joint probability depends on a second-moment parameter, not only on means.

interactions.hypothesis: After a short gap (under three weeks) fatigue and surface transition cost reduce the next leg's chance; beyond about six weeks the carryover disappears, so the link has a threshold in the gap.

interactions.hypothesis: For the same-player reading, a high surface covariance raises the probability of a second title given the first mainly when the second leg's field is thin at the top (key rivals absent or injured); against a deep field the covariance matters less because the per-match upset risk dominates, so the covariance effect scales with field concentration.

mechanism_review.summary: The live combination (KXATPWTA) pairs a named man and a named woman to both win the same major, so its probability is the intersection of two title events in separate draws. Those legs are close to independent: the only shared channels are event-level conditions (court pace, heat and roof policy, scheduling disruption) that move both draws' favourites weakly in the same direction, so the joint is essentially the product of the two marginal title probabilities, each a path product over a seven-round draw that also carries the leg player's withdrawal hazard (a withdrawal settles the pairing No). For other combination readings that are not currently listed, dependence would come from three channels. First, a shared latent strength: a player who is truly better on a surface is better on similar surfaces, which makes consecutive titles positively correlated in a way that depends on the covariance between surface ratings. Second, a shared health and availability state that persists from event to event: an injury that removes a player from one leg removes him from the next. Third, event-to-event load: winning one tournament costs matches and recovery before the next, which creates a negative correlation in some calendars, and a mutual-exclusion structure when legs name different players at the same event. A simple product of marginals misses all of these, and a joint simulation with a shared player state is needed. The contract structure adds a path-dependence: as legs resolve, the combination collapses to a conditional probability.

stages.name: Leg definition and mutual-exclusion structure
stages.description: Required first: the rules text identifies the legs. KXATPWTA names one man and one woman at the same major, so the live contract is a cross-draw pairing whose legs are nearly independent and whose joint is the product of marginals with a small shared-conditions correction; cross-surface, carry-over and health-persistence inputs apply only to a same-player reading that is not listed. Misreading the structure gives an impossible or double-counted probability.
stages.distribution: Deterministic structural classification of the intersection; wrong classification gives errors that do not depend on any data.

stages.name: Marginal title probability for each leg
stages.description: Each leg needs its own title probability from a path simulation, with the field known only up to the entries and the draw. These marginals are the baseline; their errors propagate multiplicatively into the joint.
stages.distribution: Marginals between 0.5% and 40%; their product for two or three legs is small, so relative errors matter.

stages.name: Shared latent strength across surfaces
stages.description: Conditional (same-player multi-event reading; not used by the live KXATPWTA cross-draw pairing). A player's strengths on clay and grass are correlated but not identical. The conditional probability of the second title given the first depends on the covariance of his surface-specific ratings, so a hard-court rating gap is only partly informative about grass.
stages.distribution: Correlation between surface ratings of about 0.5-0.8; joint posterior over surfaces rather than independent estimates.

stages.name: Health and availability persistence
stages.description: The probability a player is fit for the second leg given he won the first depends on injury persistence and on the load of the first leg; a long run through seven rounds raises the risk of niggles but also signals current fitness. The shared health state couples all legs for that player.
stages.distribution: Positive persistence of fitness state across consecutive events; injury hazard rises after long runs and after heavy loads.

stages.name: Event-to-event load and calendar gap
stages.description: Conditional (same-player multi-event reading; not used by the live KXATPWTA cross-draw pairing). The days between legs and the minutes on court in the first leg set recovery, and the change of surface adds a transition cost. A short gap with a long first leg lowers the second leg's probability; a long gap reduces the link.
stages.distribution: Small mean shifts in match-win probability with threshold behaviour at short gaps; interaction with surface transition.

stages.name: Joint simulation, dependence among rivals and settlement collapse
stages.description: The joint probability is obtained by simulating the legs with the shared player state, including the dependence among players in the same bracket, and the combination collapses to the remaining legs as outcomes arrive. Dependence among rivals (a top player's absence helps the others) enters through the bracket correlation.
stages.distribution: Joint distribution with positive dependence along the same player and negative dependence among rivals in the same event; resolved legs convert to conditional probabilities.

contract_review.settlement_definition: KXATPWTA is now filed here and has rules text: 'If Alexander Zverev and Iga Swiatek win the 2027 Australian Open professional men's and women's singles tennis tournaments, then the market resolves to Yes'. Each market is a named pairing of one man and one woman at the same major; Yes requires both titles. 'If either participant forfeits, withdraws from consideration, or takes any official action that removes them from being able to win both ... the market will resolve to No for that pairing', so a withdrawal is a No, not a void. The pairing dies as soon as either player loses, and after one title is won it equals the other leg's marginal. Not stated: the source of truth, and whether other combination types (same player at two events) will be listed.
contract_review.settlement_data_source: Official tournament results of the named major's men's and women's singles; not named in the sampled rules.
variants_and_edge_cases: Live structure (KXATPWTA): one man and one woman at the same major, in separate draws, so the legs are nearly independent; the joint is close to the product of the two title probabilities, with only shared-event conditions (heat policy, court pace, ball, scheduling disruption) as a weak positive link.
Withdrawal: per the rules any removal of either participant settles No for that pairing, so each leg's pre-draw withdrawal hazard enters directly as a No probability.
Leg resolution order: once one leg fails the pairing is dead; once one leg wins the pairing equals the remaining leg, so the price must be updated by conditional probability, not by marginals.
Other readings: same-player sequential combos (two majors) or two players in the same draw (mutually exclusive) are not listed; the same-player inputs here are conditional context only.

mechanism_review.summary: These contracts are not about a match; they ask whether a person takes an action inside a window, and the action is gated by health, calendar and decision. For a return or participation contract the chain is: the player's current physical state and its recovery timeline, the set of events in the window that he is eligible to enter, his or his team's decision to enter given points, prize money and fitness risk, a withdrawal hazard between entry deadline and first ball, and the definition of what counts as competing. For a retirement announcement the chain is a hazard over career stage: age, results trend, injury burden, financial and personal factors, and the habit of announcing at certain moments (end of season, a major, a farewell tour). The structure is a time-to-event process with a deadline and calendar-dependent opportunities, so the right object is a survival curve rather than a rate, and the information that moves it (an injury report, a withdrawal, a press statement) arrives in discrete jumps whose timestamp matters as much as their content.

stages.name: Physical state and recovery timeline
stages.description: The player's current health and any injury layoff set the earliest feasible return date. Recovery time depends on injury type and whether surgery was performed; public statements and training evidence narrow a wide prior. Returns are rarely earlier than stated and often later, so the timeline is right-skewed.
stages.distribution: Right-skewed time-to-return distribution (log-normal-like) conditional on injury class; Kaplan-Meier from historical layoffs with censoring for players who do not return within a season.

stages.name: Eligible events and entry pathways
stages.description: A return or participation needs a place in a draw. Entry depends on ranking versus cutoff, protected ranking, wildcard or special exemption, and acceptance list deadlines, so even a healthy player may be unable to enter a given event. The calendar within the window decides the number of attempts.
stages.distribution: Discrete set of opportunities with heterogeneous entry probability; a player under cutoff has near-zero odds without a wildcard.

stages.name: Entry decision and incentives
stages.description: Given health and eligibility, the team decides whether to commit: rankings points to defend, prize money (including first-round pay for losers), event importance and the risk of aggravating the injury. High-incentive events such as Slams make injured players start more often than ordinary events.
stages.distribution: Binary decision per event with probability rising with incentive and falling with injury severity; strongly event-dependent.

stages.name: Withdrawal and walkover hazard between entry and first ball
stages.description: After entry the player can withdraw until the draw and even after the order of play; each interval has its own hazard and each has different information (practice sessions, press conferences). The 'competes' definition determines whether a withdrawal after the draw ends the contract at No.
stages.distribution: Hazard concentrated in the 48 hours before the first scheduled match; withdrawal probability increases with recent layoff and reported complaint.

stages.name: Retirement announcement hazard
stages.description: For the retirement contract the process is different: a hazard of announcing retirement as a function of age, career length, ranking trajectory, injury load and personal statements. Announcements cluster around the end of the season, after major tournaments and at farewell events, and are rarely made out of a clear sky for top players still winning.
stages.distribution: Low-probability annual hazard for most players, rising past 33-35 and with ranking decline; right tail for injury-forced announcements.

stages.name: Settlement definition and source
stages.description: What counts as competing, which data source decides, and the time of resolution determine edge cases: a walkover in round one, a retirement after one game, an announcement with a delayed effective date. The retirement base rate and match-level settlement wording matter for how in-event outcomes are recorded.
stages.distribution: Definition-driven discrete edge cases; probability mass small but systematic around Slam first rounds.

stages.name: Return from completed retirement
stages.description: KXWTASERENA asks whether a player who has already retired competes in any WTA official tournament in 2026. The chain is: a personal decision to return, an anti-doping re-registration with advance notice that fixes the earliest eligible date, an entry route without a ranking (wildcard, special exemption or a doubles slot with a partner), and then the first match before the window closes. Each link is observable only through announcements, and the notice period alone can make the event impossible late in the year.
stages.distribution: Near-degenerate at zero absent a public re-entry step; after a step, a time-to-event hazard truncated by the window end, with the notice period acting as a hard lower bound on time to first match.

opponent_matchup.note: Participation and retirement-announcement outcomes do not depend on an opponent; the only opponent-dependent element is first-round walkover timing, which is part of the withdrawal hazard.

coaching_scheme.note: Coach and team decisions affect scheduling but are not observable as separate variables; their effect passes through public statements and the entry decision captured by incentives and news.

environment.note: Weather, heat and rain delays do not decide whether a player enters, returns or announces retirement within a window; they affect match timing only, and in-match retirement conditions are not part of these three contracts.

game_context_script.note: No game script is involved; a participation or announcement contract is a calendar event rather than a match state, and the in-match retirement is covered under the availability inputs.

pace_volume.note: There is no volume count; the quantity is binary within a window, and the number of eligible events is an opportunity set handled under the calendar input.

efficiency_conversion.note: No per-opportunity conversion rate exists beyond the entry decision probability, which is covered under incentive and availability inputs.

contract_review.settlement_definition: Four event definitions share this archetype. KXATPCOMPETE settles Yes if the named player 'competes in the 2026 US Open men's singles tennis tournament' (participation in a named event, with 'competes' undefined in the sample: entry, appearing in the draw, or playing a ball). KXATPRETURN settles Yes if the player 'competes in an ATP Match after May 19, 2026 and before September 1, 2026', with a note that the US Open counts, so it is a time-to-return event inside a closed window. KXATPRETIRE settles Yes if the player announces retirement before 2027, with the note that the retirement 'must be intended to be effective immediately or prior to 2027'. KXWTASERENA settles Yes if 'Serena Williams competes in any WTA official tournament in 2026', a comeback from completed retirement with no secondary text. None of the sampled texts states what happens on a walkover, a first-point retirement, or a late withdrawal, nor the named source of truth.
contract_review.settlement_data_source: Not named in the sampled rules; ATP Tour official draws, results and public statements are the natural sources (not verified).
variants_and_edge_cases: A walkover versus a played match: whether a player entered but withdrawing before the first ball 'competes' is not stated for KXATPCOMPETE; the match-level rules treat a pre-start walkover as non-occurrence, which points to No but is not confirmed.
In-match retirement after the first ball: competing has plainly started, so a player who retires in the first round likely counts for COMPETE and RETURN, but the rules do not say so.

Retirement announcement scope: an announcement made before 2027 that the player will retire at the end of 2027 does not meet the 'effective immediately or prior to 2027' note; a statement of 'considering retirement' is not an announcement.

Time windows with clock ambiguity: window endpoints (May 19 and September 1) are dates without a time zone or timestamp, and the issued-date condition 'after Issuance' used by the major series is not visible here.

Eligible-event scope for KXATPRETURN: the note makes the US Open an ATP Match explicitly, but ATP Challenger, team-event ties (Davis Cup, Laver Cup), exhibitions, Olympic and qualifying matches are not addressed; ten.eligible_event_calendar must be built for the ATP Tour main-draw events only until scope is clarified (rp_atp_match_scope).

Verification level: the rules text was read for all four series, but 'competes' is undefined, the source of truth is unnamed and the announcement channel is not visible, so the contract is only partially verified.

Return from completed retirement (KXWTASERENA): the player is not injured but retired, so the path runs through a re-entry decision, anti-doping re-registration notice and a wildcard or protected-ranking entry; whether doubles, a WTA 125 event or a Grand Slam (ITF-sanctioned, on the WTA calendar) is a 'WTA official tournament' is not stated.
